questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: Which statement about Cisco TrustSec Security Group Tags (SGTs) is correct?

options.A: SGTs classify traffic and enable policy enforcement independent of IP addressing or topology
options.B: SGTs are assigned based on the destination IP address only
options.C: SGTs are only usable with MACsec encryption enabled
options.D: SGTs replace the need for VLANs entirely

questions.explanation_es: Las SGT (Security Group Tags) de TrustSec clasifican el tráfico según el rol/identidad del usuario o dispositivo, permitiendo aplicar políticas de segmentación independientemente de la IP o la topología física. No dependen de VLANs ni requieren MACsec.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: At which layer does MACsec (802.1AE) provide encryption?

options.A: Layer 4, encrypting TCP/UDP segments
options.B: Layer 3, encrypting the IP header and payload
options.C: Layer 2, encrypting Ethernet frames hop-by-hop between adjacent devices
options.D: Layer 7, encrypting application data end-to-end

questions.explanation_es: MACsec opera en Capa 2 y cifra los frames Ethernet salto por salto (hop-by-hop) entre dispositivos adyacentes directamente conectados. Cada enlace tiene su propia asociación de seguridad; NO es cifrado end-to-end como IPsec.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: A network has MACsec enabled between Switch A and Switch B, and separately between Switch B and Switch C. If a frame travels from A to C through B, what happens to the encryption?

options.A: The frame remains encrypted with the same key throughout the path
options.B: MACsec cannot be used across more than one hop
options.C: The frame is encrypted only once at the source and decrypted only at the final destination
options.D: The frame is decrypted at B, processed, and re-encrypted with a different session key before forwarding to C

questions.explanation_es: Como MACsec es hop-by-hop, en cada salto el frame se descifra, se procesa/conmuta en texto claro dentro del dispositivo, y se vuelve a cifrar con una asociación de seguridad distinta antes del siguiente salto. No hay una sola sesión cifrada de extremo a extremo.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: What is the role of the Security Association Protocol (SAP) or MKA (MACsec Key Agreement) in a MACsec deployment?

options.A: It performs deep packet inspection on encrypted traffic
options.B: It routes traffic between TrustSec domains
options.C: It assigns SGTs to endpoints
options.D: It negotiates and manages the encryption keys used to secure the point-to-point link

questions.explanation_es: MKA (MACsec Key Agreement, definido en 802.1X-2010) es el protocolo que negocia y renueva las claves de cifrado usadas por MACsec en el enlace punto a punto. La asignación de SGT es una función distinta, propia de TrustSec/ISE.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: In a TrustSec architecture, what device typically performs SGT propagation over links that do not support inline tagging?

options.A: SGT is embedded in the DSCP field
options.B: SGT is converted into a VLAN ID automatically
options.C: SGT is carried using SXP (SGT Exchange Protocol) to propagate IP-to-SGT bindings to devices without hardware support
options.D: SGT is dropped and traffic is untagged

questions.explanation_es: SXP (SGT Exchange Protocol) permite propagar los bindings IP-a-SGT hacia dispositivos que no soportan el etiquetado inline (in-line tagging) en hardware, típicamente entre switches de acceso más antiguos y el enforcement point.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: Which component enforces TrustSec policy based on SGT-to-SGT communication rules?

options.A: The STP root bridge
options.B: The DHCP relay agent
options.C: The Security Group ACL (SGACL), applied at the enforcement point
options.D: The VTP server

questions.explanation_es: Las SGACL (Security Group ACLs) son las que definen y aplican qué comunicación está permitida entre grupos (SGT origen -> SGT destino), y se aplican en el punto de enforcement (generalmente el switch de egreso o el firewall).

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: Which statement correctly compares MACsec and IPsec?

options.A: MACsec secures Layer 2 links hop-by-hop; IPsec can secure traffic end-to-end across Layer 3 routed paths
options.B: MACsec requires a VPN gateway, while IPsec does not
options.C: Both provide identical end-to-end encryption across multiple routed hops
options.D: IPsec only works on wireless links, while MACsec only works on wired links

questions.explanation_es: MACsec cifra tráfico de Capa 2 en cada enlace físico directo (hop-by-hop), mientras que IPsec puede establecer túneles end-to-end sobre Capa 3, atravesando múltiples saltos enrutados sin descifrarse en cada uno.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: Which is a primary benefit of TrustSec's SGT-based segmentation compared to traditional VLAN-based segmentation?

options.A: It only works within a single VLAN
options.B: It eliminates the need for any access control policy
options.C: It decouples policy from IP addressing/topology, simplifying segmentation across the network without redesigning VLANs/subnets
options.D: It requires re-IPing the entire network

questions.explanation_es: El valor de TrustSec es que la política de segmentación se basa en la identidad/rol (SGT), no en la IP o VLAN, por lo que se puede segmentar sin rediseñar el esquema de direccionamiento o de VLANs.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: What happens to MACsec-protected traffic if it needs to traverse an untrusted, non-MACsec-capable Layer 2 device in the middle of the path?

options.A: The chain of hop-by-hop protection is broken at that device, since MACsec requires MACsec-capable devices at every hop
options.B: Nothing changes, IPsec takes over automatically
options.C: MACsec automatically tunnels through the device transparently
options.D: The device automatically upgrades to support MACsec

questions.explanation_es: Como MACsec depende de asociaciones de seguridad por enlace entre dispositivos adyacentes que lo soportan, un salto intermedio sin capacidad MACsec rompe la cadena de protección hop-by-hop en ese punto.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: Which Cisco platform typically acts as the policy administration point (PAP) in a TrustSec deployment, defining SGTs and SGACL policies?

options.A: Cisco WLC exclusively
options.B: Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE)
options.C: Cisco IOS XR route processor
options.D: Cisco Catalyst Center only

questions.explanation_es: Cisco ISE (Identity Services Engine) es típicamente el punto de administración de políticas (PAP) en TrustSec: define SGTs, políticas SGACL y las distribuye a los enforcement points.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: In YANG, what is the primary distinction between a 'list' and a 'leaf-list'?

options.A: A 'leaf-list' requires a key statement, while a 'list' never does
options.B: They are functionally identical, just named differently for readability
options.C: A 'list' contains multiple instances of complex data with one or more child nodes (potentially with keys); a 'leaf-list' contains multiple instances of a single simple leaf value
options.D: A 'list' can only hold strings; a 'leaf-list' can hold any type

questions.explanation_es: Un 'list' agrupa múltiples instancias de una estructura de datos compleja (con uno o más nodos hijos, normalmente identificadas por una 'key'); un 'leaf-list' es simplemente una colección de valores simples de un único leaf, sin estructura interna adicional.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: What is the main purpose of a YANG data model in network automation?

options.A: To provide a standardized, structured, and vendor-neutral (or vendor-specific) definition of configuration and operational data for programmatic access
options.B: To act as a routing protocol
options.C: To compress configuration files for storage
options.D: To replace the CLI as the only way to configure a device

questions.explanation_es: YANG es un lenguaje de modelado de datos que define de forma estructurada y estandarizada cómo se representan los datos de configuración y estado operativo de un dispositivo, permitiendo el acceso programático consistente vía NETCONF/RESTCONF.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: Which statement about YANG 'container' is correct?

options.A: A container can only contain leaf-list elements
options.B: A container is equivalent to a leaf with multiple values
options.C: A container is always mandatory and cannot be nested
options.D: A container groups related nodes together but does not itself hold a value; it's an organizational structure

questions.explanation_es: Un 'container' en YANG agrupa nodos relacionados (leafs, lists, otros containers) de forma jerárquica y organizativa; en sí mismo no almacena un valor, solo estructura los datos.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: What are the two main types of YANG modules used with NETCONF/RESTCONF for network devices?

options.A: XML models and JSON models
options.B: Only vendor-native models exist
options.C: Native (vendor-specific) models and Open/Standard models (such as those from IETF or OpenConfig)
options.D: Only OpenConfig models are valid for Cisco devices

questions.explanation_es: Existen modelos YANG nativos (específicos del fabricante, ej. Cisco-IOS-XE-native) y modelos abiertos/estándar (IETF, OpenConfig), que buscan ofrecer una representación común entre distintos fabricantes.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: Which of the following is a key benefit of using YANG models compared to screen-scraping CLI output for automation?

options.A: YANG eliminates the need for any authentication
options.B: YANG only works with SNMP
options.C: YANG provides a structured, machine-readable schema with defined data types, reducing parsing errors compared to unstructured CLI text
options.D: YANG requires more bandwidth than CLI scraping in all cases

questions.explanation_es: El beneficio central de YANG es que define un esquema estructurado con tipos de datos definidos, lo cual es mucho más confiable de procesar de forma programática que hacer 'screen-scraping' de salidas de CLI que pueden cambiar de formato entre versiones.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: In a YANG list definition, what is the purpose of the 'key' statement?

options.A: It encrypts the list data
options.B: It defines the default value for the entire list
options.C: It defines which leaf(s) uniquely identify each entry/instance within the list
options.D: It is only used for leaf-lists, not lists

questions.explanation_es: El statement 'key' en un 'list' de YANG especifica qué leaf o combinación de leafs identifica de forma única cada instancia/entrada dentro de esa lista, similar a una clave primaria.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: Which protocol(s) commonly use YANG models to exchange configuration and operational data?

options.A: Only SNMP
options.B: Only Telnet
options.C: Only BGP
options.D: NETCONF and RESTCONF

questions.explanation_es: NETCONF y RESTCONF son los protocolos de gestión que utilizan modelos YANG como esquema de datos para representar la configuración y el estado operativo intercambiado con el dispositivo.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: What does the YANG 'rpc' statement define?

options.A: A routing protocol configuration
options.B: A read-only leaf value
options.C: A container used only for statistics
options.D: A remote procedure call operation with defined input and output parameters, such as a reboot or clear-counters action

questions.explanation_es: El statement 'rpc' en YANG define una operación de tipo llamada a procedimiento remoto, con parámetros de entrada y salida definidos (por ejemplo, una acción de reinicio o de limpieza de contadores), distinta de la simple configuración de datos.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: Which statement about YANG data modeling and vendor interoperability is accurate?

options.A: Native YANG models guarantee full interoperability across all vendors
options.B: YANG models are identical regardless of whether they are native or open
options.C: Only IETF models can be used with NETCONF
options.D: OpenConfig/IETF models aim to provide a common, vendor-neutral schema, while native models are vendor-specific and may differ significantly between platforms

questions.explanation_es: Los modelos abiertos (OpenConfig/IETF) buscan ofrecer un esquema común entre fabricantes, mientras que los modelos nativos son específicos de cada plataforma y pueden variar bastante entre sí, lo que reduce la portabilidad de la automatización basada en ellos.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: A YANG leaf-list named 'dns-server' contains the values '8.8.8.8' and '1.1.1.1'. If you needed to instead model each DNS server with both an IP address and a description, which construct would be more appropriate?

options.A: Use a 'list' with a key (e.g., the IP) and child leafs for the IP and description, since leaf-list only supports single simple values
options.B: Keep using leaf-list, since it already supports multiple attributes per entry
options.C: Use a single leaf with a comma-separated string
options.D: Use a container with no children

questions.explanation_es: Cuando cada entrada necesita más de un atributo (IP + descripción), se requiere un 'list' con una key y leafs hijos, ya que un 'leaf-list' solo puede almacenar valores simples de un único tipo, uno por entrada.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: What type of API does Cisco Catalyst Center primarily expose for northbound programmatic access?

options.A: Only CLI-based scripting
options.B: A proprietary binary protocol
options.C: SOAP-based APIs exclusively
options.D: RESTful APIs using HTTPS with JSON payloads

questions.explanation_es: Cisco Catalyst Center expone principalmente APIs RESTful sobre HTTPS con payloads en JSON, permitiendo integraciones northbound con sistemas de terceros y automatización.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: Which category of Catalyst Center APIs would you use to retrieve inventory information about devices managed by the platform?

options.A: Only SD-WAN Manager APIs
options.B: Only northbound SSH APIs
options.C: SNMP trap APIs
options.D: Intent APIs / Discovery and Inventory APIs

questions.explanation_es: Catalyst Center ofrece Intent APIs, entre ellas las de Discovery e Inventory, que permiten consultar la lista de dispositivos descubiertos y gestionados, su estado, y detalles asociados.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: What authentication mechanism is typically used first when interacting with Cisco Catalyst Center's REST API?

options.A: No authentication is required for any API call
options.B: Kerberos exclusively
options.C: Obtaining an authentication token via a POST request with credentials, then using that token in subsequent API calls
options.D: Only client-side certificates, with no username/password support

questions.explanation_es: El flujo típico es enviar credenciales (usuario/contraseña) en una solicitud POST para obtener un token de autenticación (X-Auth-Token), que luego se incluye en el header de las llamadas API subsecuentes.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: How do Cisco SD-WAN Manager (vManage) APIs differ in purpose from Catalyst Center APIs, at a high level?

options.A: Catalyst Center has no APIs related to network provisioning
options.B: They are functionally identical and interchangeable
options.C: SD-WAN Manager APIs are SOAP-only
options.D: SD-WAN Manager APIs focus on managing and monitoring the SD-WAN fabric (templates, policies, device onboarding), while Catalyst Center APIs focus on the campus/branch enterprise network (intent-based provisioning, assurance)

questions.explanation_es: Ambos son controladores con APIs RESTful, pero SD-WAN Manager gestiona específicamente el fabric SD-WAN (plantillas, políticas, onboarding de dispositivos SD-WAN), mientras que Catalyst Center gestiona la red empresarial de campus/sucursal con un enfoque de intención (intent-based) y aseguramiento (assurance).

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: Which Catalyst Center API capability allows you to trigger provisioning of a network intent, such as applying a template to a device?

options.A: Intent APIs that support both GET (read) and POST/PUT (create/update) operations for network configuration and provisioning
options.B: Only APIs for user management
options.C: Only export APIs for reporting
options.D: Assurance-only read APIs

questions.explanation_es: Las Intent APIs de Catalyst Center soportan tanto operaciones de lectura (GET) como de escritura (POST/PUT) para desencadenar acciones de provisioning e intención sobre la red, no solo consultas.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: Which statement best describes Catalyst Center's Assurance APIs?

options.A: They do not exist; assurance data is CLI-only
options.B: They are used exclusively to change VLAN configurations
options.C: They are used only for firmware upgrades
options.D: They provide access to health scores, telemetry, and analytics data about network and client performance

questions.explanation_es: Las Assurance APIs de Catalyst Center exponen datos de salud de red, telemetría y analítica sobre el desempeño de la red y de los clientes, útiles para monitoreo y troubleshooting proactivo.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: What is a typical use case for integrating a third-party ITSM (IT Service Management) tool with Catalyst Center APIs?

options.A: Replacing the need for network devices entirely
options.B: Only for billing purposes
options.C: Automatically creating a ticket or workflow when Catalyst Center detects a network issue via its Assurance/Event APIs
options.D: ITSM tools cannot integrate with Catalyst Center in any way

questions.explanation_es: Un caso de uso común es que un evento o problema detectado por las Assurance/Event APIs de Catalyst Center dispare automáticamente la creación de un ticket o flujo de trabajo en una herramienta ITSM externa (ej. ServiceNow).

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: Which of these is an advantage of using Catalyst Center APIs over configuring devices individually via CLI?

options.A: APIs are slower than manual CLI configuration in every case
options.B: APIs allow centralized, intent-based, and repeatable automation across many devices at once, reducing manual per-device configuration
options.C: APIs require more manual steps per device than CLI
options.D: APIs cannot scale beyond a single device

questions.explanation_es: El principal beneficio es la automatización centralizada y basada en intención, aplicable de forma repetible a muchos dispositivos a la vez, reduciendo la configuración manual dispositivo por dispositivo.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: When calling Catalyst Center's Intent API to get the list of network devices, what is the typical HTTP method used?

options.A: OPTIONS only
options.B: GET
options.C: DELETE
options.D: PATCH only

questions.explanation_es: Para consultar información (como la lista de dispositivos de red), el método HTTP típico es GET, que se usa para operaciones de lectura sin modificar datos.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: What format does Catalyst Center typically use for API request and response bodies?

options.A: YAML exclusively
options.B: Plain text only
options.C: CSV
options.D: JSON

questions.explanation_es: Catalyst Center utiliza JSON como formato estándar para los cuerpos de las solicitudes y respuestas de su API REST.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: According to RFC 8040, what is the well-known base URI path used to discover the RESTCONF API entry point on a device?

options.A: /netconf/rest
options.B: /.well-known/host-meta
options.C: /restconf
options.D: /api/v1/restconf

questions.explanation_es: Según RFC 8040, el punto de entrada base de RESTCONF es '/restconf' (el dispositivo puede anunciar la ruta exacta vía /.well-known/host-meta, pero '/restconf' es la ruta convencional y comúnmente usada por defecto).

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: Which HTTP status code does RESTCONF typically return when a new resource is successfully created via a POST request?

options.A: 204 No Content
options.B: 201 Created
options.C: 404 Not Found
options.D: 200 OK

questions.explanation_es: Cuando un POST crea exitosamente un nuevo recurso, el código correcto es 201 Created. 200 OK se usa típicamente para respuestas exitosas a GET/PUT donde no se crea un recurso nuevo con Location, y 204 No Content para operaciones exitosas sin cuerpo de respuesta.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: Which HTTP method does RESTCONF use to completely replace an existing configuration resource?

options.A: OPTIONS
options.B: HEAD
options.C: GET
options.D: PUT

questions.explanation_es: PUT se usa en RESTCONF para reemplazar completamente un recurso de configuración existente (o crearlo si no existe, retornando 201 en ese caso). PATCH se usaría para una modificación parcial.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: RESTCONF and NETCONF both use YANG data models, but what is a key architectural difference between them?

options.A: RESTCONF uses HTTP(S) with a stateless request/response model, while NETCONF uses a session-based protocol typically over SSH with an RPC-based XML exchange
options.B: NETCONF only supports read operations, RESTCONF supports both read and write
options.C: RESTCONF cannot use YANG models, only NETCONF can
options.D: They are exactly the same protocol with different names

questions.explanation_es: RESTCONF opera sobre HTTP(S) de forma stateless (sin sesión persistente), usando verbos HTTP estándar; NETCONF establece una sesión persistente (típicamente sobre SSH) e intercambia mensajes RPC en XML. Ambos pueden usar los mismos modelos YANG subyacentes.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: Which media types are commonly supported in the Accept/Content-Type headers of a RESTCONF request?

options.A: Only application/octet-stream
options.B: application/yang-data+json and application/yang-data+xml
options.C: Only multipart/form-data
options.D: Only text/plain

questions.explanation_es: RESTCONF soporta representaciones en JSON y XML mediante los media types específicos application/yang-data+json y application/yang-data+xml, indicados en los headers Accept y Content-Type.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: What HTTP status code indicates a successful DELETE operation in RESTCONF, with no content returned?

options.A: 200 OK
options.B: 301 Moved Permanently
options.C: 204 No Content
options.D: 201 Created

questions.explanation_es: Una operación DELETE exitosa que no retorna cuerpo de respuesta se indica típicamente con el código 204 No Content.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: In RESTCONF, which HTTP method is used to perform a partial modification (merge) of an existing configuration resource rather than replacing it entirely?

options.A: HEAD
options.B: PATCH
options.C: DELETE
options.D: PUT

questions.explanation_es: PATCH se utiliza para aplicar una modificación parcial (merge) sobre un recurso existente, a diferencia de PUT que reemplaza el recurso completo.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: Which datastore does RESTCONF operate against, in contrast to NETCONF's separate running/candidate/startup datastores?

options.A: RESTCONF requires a candidate datastore for every operation
options.B: RESTCONF only supports the startup datastore
options.C: RESTCONF has no concept of a datastore
options.D: RESTCONF operates directly against a single conceptual 'running' datastore, without a separate candidate datastore commit model

questions.explanation_es: A diferencia de NETCONF, que puede trabajar con datastores separados (running, candidate, startup) y requiere un commit explícito, RESTCONF opera directamente sobre un datastore conceptual único (equivalente a 'running'), aplicando cambios de forma inmediata.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: If a RESTCONF client sends a malformed JSON body that doesn't validate against the YANG schema, what type of HTTP status code range would you expect in the response?

options.A: 2xx (Success)
options.B: 1xx (Informational)
options.C: 3xx (Redirection) always
options.D: 4xx (Client Error), such as 400 Bad Request

questions.explanation_es: Un error del cliente, como un JSON malformado o que no valida contra el esquema YANG, típicamente resulta en un código 4xx, como 400 Bad Request, indicando que el problema está en la solicitud enviada.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: Which of the following correctly reflects the RESTCONF URI structure for accessing configuration data under the base path?

options.A: Data and operations both use /restconf/yang-library/
options.B: There is no distinction; everything uses /restconf/rpc/
options.C: /restconf/data/{...} is used to access data resources (config and state), and /restconf/operations/{rpc-name} is used to invoke RPC operations
options.D: /restconf/operations/{rpc-name} is used for data resources, and /restconf/data/{...} is used for RPC operations

questions.explanation_es: En RESTCONF, '/restconf/data/{...}' se usa para acceder a recursos de datos (configuración y estado), mientras que '/restconf/operations/{rpc-name}' se usa para invocar operaciones RPC definidas en el modelo YANG.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: What is the primary function of a virtual switch (vSwitch) in a virtualized/hypervisor environment?

options.A: To provide storage replication between hosts
options.B: To perform Layer 3 routing exclusively, with no Layer 2 function
options.C: To replace the need for physical switches in the entire data center
options.D: To switch Ethernet frames between virtual machines on the same host, and between VMs and the physical network via the host's physical NICs

questions.explanation_es: Un vSwitch conmuta tramas Ethernet entre las máquinas virtuales que corren en el mismo host, y entre esas VMs y la red física a través de las NICs físicas del host (uplinks), funcionando principalmente en Capa 2.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: What does Open vSwitch (OVS) support that distinguishes it from a very basic vSwitch?

options.A: OVS requires proprietary hardware to function
options.B: OVS cannot support VLANs
options.C: OVS supports advanced features such as OpenFlow programmability, VXLAN/GRE tunneling, and fine-grained flow-based forwarding
options.D: OVS only works with a single hypervisor vendor and cannot be programmed

questions.explanation_es: Open vSwitch es un vSwitch de código abierto que soporta características avanzadas como programabilidad vía OpenFlow, tunneling VXLAN/GRE, y reenvío basado en flujos (flow-based forwarding), yendo más allá de un vSwitch básico.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: In VMware vSphere, what is the difference between a Standard vSwitch and a Distributed vSwitch (vDS)?

options.A: A Distributed vSwitch cannot support port groups
options.B: A Standard vSwitch spans multiple hosts automatically
options.C: They are functionally identical
options.D: A Standard vSwitch is configured and managed per individual host, while a Distributed vSwitch provides centralized configuration and consistent policy across multiple hosts in a cluster

questions.explanation_es: El Standard vSwitch se configura de forma independiente en cada host ESXi, mientras que el Distributed vSwitch (vDS) ofrece una configuración centralizada y consistente que abarca múltiples hosts dentro de un clúster, simplificando la administración.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: What is a 'port group' in the context of a VMware vSwitch?

options.A: A logical grouping of virtual ports on the vSwitch that share the same network policy, such as VLAN tagging and security settings
options.B: A physical port on the ESXi host's network card
options.C: A routing table entry
options.D: A group of physical switches connected together

questions.explanation_es: Un port group es una agrupación lógica de puertos virtuales en el vSwitch que comparten la misma política de red (VLAN, seguridad, shaping de tráfico, etc.), y a la cual se conectan las vNICs de las VMs.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: Which security feature, when misconfigured or disabled on a vSwitch port group, could allow a VM to send frames claiming to be from a different MAC address than its configured vNIC?

options.A: Jumbo frames
options.B: Forged Transmits protection
options.C: NIC teaming
options.D: VLAN tagging

questions.explanation_es: 'Forged Transmits' es una política de seguridad del vSwitch que, cuando está habilitada (rechazando), bloquea que una VM envíe tramas con una dirección MAC de origen distinta a la configurada en su vNIC. Si se deshabilita, permite ese comportamiento (potencialmente malicioso).

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: How does a vSwitch typically learn which VM (virtual port) is associated with a given source MAC address?

options.A: Dynamically, similar to a physical switch, by examining the source MAC address of frames received from each virtual port
options.B: vSwitches do not perform MAC learning at all
options.C: By querying DNS for MAC-to-port mappings
options.D: Through static configuration only, never dynamically

questions.explanation_es: Al igual que un switch físico, el vSwitch aprende dinámicamente qué puerto virtual corresponde a cada dirección MAC observando las tramas recibidas desde cada puerto y registrando la MAC de origen.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: What is a key advantage of using Open vSwitch (OVS) in an SDN/NFV environment compared to a traditional vendor-specific vSwitch?

options.A: OVS is open-source, widely supported across hypervisors/cloud platforms, and integrates well with SDN controllers via OpenFlow, aiding portability and centralized control
options.B: OVS is only usable in bare-metal environments, not virtualized ones
options.C: OVS cannot integrate with any SDN controller
options.D: OVS eliminates the need for any physical network

questions.explanation_es: OVS es de código abierto, ampliamente soportado en distintos hipervisores y plataformas cloud, y se integra bien con controladores SDN vía OpenFlow, lo que facilita portabilidad y control centralizado del plano de reenvío en entornos SDN/NFV.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: Which statement about VLAN tagging on a vSwitch port group (Virtual Switch Tagging, VST mode) is correct?

options.A: The physical switch removes the tag before it reaches the vSwitch
options.B: The vSwitch tags/untags frames with the port group's configured VLAN ID; the VM's guest OS is unaware of VLAN tagging
options.C: VLAN tagging is impossible in a virtualized environment
options.D: The VM's guest OS must be configured to add the VLAN tag itself

questions.explanation_es: En modo VST (Virtual Switch Tagging), el propio vSwitch añade/quita la etiqueta VLAN configurada en el port group; el sistema operativo invitado de la VM no necesita saber nada sobre VLANs, ya que el tagging ocurre de forma transparente en el vSwitch.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: In a hypervisor host with multiple physical NICs configured as an uplink team on a vSwitch, what is the primary purpose of this configuration?

options.A: To convert the vSwitch into a Layer 3 router
options.B: To eliminate the need for MAC learning
options.C: To provide redundancy and/or load balancing of traffic leaving the host toward the physical network
options.D: To disable all outbound traffic from the VMs

questions.explanation_es: Agrupar múltiples NICs físicas como uplinks en team en un vSwitch provee redundancia (failover) y/o balanceo de carga del tráfico saliente hacia la red física, de forma similar a un EtherChannel.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: Why can't traffic between two VMs on the same vSwitch and same port group typically be inspected by a traditional external physical firewall or IPS without additional configuration?

options.A: Because vSwitches encrypt all traffic by default
options.B: Because VMs on the same port group cannot communicate at all
options.C: Because the vSwitch always routes such traffic through Layer 3
options.D: Because that intra-host, intra-port-group traffic is switched locally within the vSwitch and never leaves the host to reach the physical network where the external device sits

questions.explanation_es: El tráfico entre dos VMs en el mismo vSwitch y mismo port group se conmuta localmente dentro del propio vSwitch, sin salir físicamente del host hacia la red externa, por lo que un firewall/IPS físico tradicional no lo ve a menos que se use algo como un firewall virtual o se fuerce el tráfico a salir (hairpin).

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: In a VXLAN EVPN fabric, what mechanism is primarily used to distribute MAC-to-VTEP (endpoint) mapping information, replacing traditional flood-and-learn?

options.A: BGP EVPN control plane, which advertises MAC and MAC/IP routes between VTEPs
options.B: ARP flooding only
options.C: Spanning Tree Protocol (STP)
options.D: OSPF

questions.explanation_es: En VXLAN con EVPN, el plano de control BGP EVPN es el que distribuye las asociaciones MAC-a-VTEP (y MAC/IP) entre los VTEPs mediante rutas EVPN tipo 2, eliminando la necesidad de flood-and-learn tradicional para el aprendizaje de MACs remotas.

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: What does 'BUM' traffic stand for in the context of VXLAN, and why is it a design challenge?

options.A: Broadcast, Unknown-unicast, and Multicast traffic; it needs to be replicated/delivered to all relevant VTEPs, requiring either multicast underlay or ingress replication
options.B: Bidirectional Unicast Messaging; it refers to control-plane BGP sessions
options.C: Bandwidth Usage Monitoring; it is only relevant for QoS
options.D: Backup Unicast Mode; it is a failover mechanism for VTEPs

questions.explanation_es: BUM significa Broadcast, Unknown-unicast y Multicast traffic. En VXLAN es un desafío porque, al no existir un dominio de broadcast Capa 2 nativo entre VTEPs remotos, este tráfico debe replicarse hacia todos los VTEPs relevantes, típicamente mediante multicast en el underlay o mediante ingress replication (unicast) por cada VTEP destino.

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: In a VXLAN EVPN deployment using ingress replication (head-end replication) instead of multicast underlay, how is BUM traffic handled?

options.A: BUM traffic is converted to unicast ARP requests only, with no other flooding
options.B: The underlay automatically enables PIM regardless of configuration
options.C: The ingress VTEP makes multiple unicast copies of the BUM frame, one for each remote VTEP that needs to receive it
options.D: BUM traffic is simply dropped since multicast is unavailable

questions.explanation_es: Con ingress replication (head-end replication), el VTEP de ingreso genera copias unicast individuales de la trama BUM, una por cada VTEP remoto que necesita recibirla, evitando la necesidad de multicast en el underlay a costa de mayor carga en el VTEP de origen.

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: What is the function of a VTEP (VXLAN Tunnel Endpoint)?

options.A: It performs only Layer 1 signal regeneration
options.B: It encapsulates and decapsulates Ethernet frames into/from VXLAN (UDP) packets, bridging the Layer 2 overlay to the Layer 3 underlay
options.C: It replaces the need for an IP underlay entirely
options.D: It is a pure Layer 3 routing protocol with no encapsulation role

questions.explanation_es: El VTEP (VXLAN Tunnel Endpoint) es el que encapsula tramas Ethernet en paquetes VXLAN sobre UDP (y las desencapsula en el destino), permitiendo que un dominio Layer 2 overlay viaje sobre un underlay Layer 3 enrutado.

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: How does EVPN Type-2 route advertisement help reduce unknown-unicast flooding in a VXLAN fabric?

options.A: Type-2 routes only advertise IP prefixes, not MAC addresses
options.B: Type-2 routes are used exclusively for multicast group membership
options.C: Type-2 routes disable all flooding permanently, including for genuinely new/unknown hosts
options.D: Type-2 routes advertise MAC (and optionally IP) addresses along with the originating VTEP, allowing remote VTEPs to learn reachability via BGP control plane instead of relying on data-plane flood-and-learn

questions.explanation_es: Las rutas EVPN Tipo 2 anuncian direcciones MAC (y opcionalmente la IP asociada) junto con el VTEP de origen vía BGP, permitiendo que los VTEPs remotos aprendan la ubicación de los hosts por el plano de control en lugar de depender del flood-and-learn tradicional del plano de datos, reduciendo así el tráfico de unknown-unicast.

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: What is the purpose of the VNI (VXLAN Network Identifier) field in a VXLAN header?

options.A: It identifies the underlay routing protocol being used
options.B: It identifies the specific Layer 2 overlay segment/broadcast domain, similar in concept to a VLAN ID but with a much larger address space (24 bits)
options.C: It is used only for QoS marking
options.D: It specifies the destination VTEP's physical MAC address

questions.explanation_es: El VNI (VXLAN Network Identifier) identifica el segmento de overlay Capa 2 (dominio de broadcast), de forma conceptualmente similar a una VLAN ID, pero con un espacio de direccionamiento de 24 bits (hasta ~16 millones de segmentos), muy superior a las 4094 VLANs tradicionales.

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: In a multicast-based VXLAN underlay (without EVPN), how is BUM traffic typically delivered to all VTEPs interested in a given VNI?

options.A: BUM traffic uses OSPF flooding instead of multicast
options.B: BUM traffic is dropped since VXLAN cannot use multicast
options.C: Each VNI is mapped to a multicast group in the underlay; BUM traffic is sent to that multicast group, and PIM handles replication to all VTEPs that have joined it
options.D: BUM traffic is always sent via unicast to every VTEP individually, regardless of multicast availability

questions.explanation_es: En un underlay multicast (flood-and-learn clásico sin EVPN), cada VNI se asocia a un grupo multicast en el underlay; el tráfico BUM se envía a ese grupo, y PIM se encarga de replicarlo hacia todos los VTEPs que se unieron (join) a ese grupo, evitando el envío unicast individual.

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: Which EVPN route type is used to advertise IP prefix reachability (useful for inter-subnet/symmetric IRB routing) rather than individual host MAC/IP bindings?

options.A: Type 3 (Inclusive Multicast Ethernet Tag)
options.B: Type 1 (Ethernet Auto-Discovery)
options.C: Type 2 (MAC/IP Advertisement)
options.D: Type 5 (IP Prefix route)

questions.explanation_es: Las rutas EVPN Tipo 5 (IP Prefix routes) se usan para anunciar alcanzabilidad de prefijos IP, típicamente para enrutamiento inter-subred (symmetric IRB), en lugar de bindings individuales de host como hace Tipo 2 (MAC/IP Advertisement).

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: What advantage does BGP EVPN provide for ARP suppression in a VXLAN fabric?

options.A: ARP suppression requires disabling BGP EVPN entirely
options.B: Local VTEPs can respond to ARP requests for known remote hosts using information learned via EVPN Type-2 routes, avoiding the need to flood ARP requests across the fabric
options.C: ARP suppression only works with IPv6, never IPv4
options.D: BGP EVPN has no relationship to ARP handling

questions.explanation_es: Gracias a que los VTEPs aprenden los bindings MAC/IP de hosts remotos vía rutas EVPN Tipo 2, un VTEP local puede responder directamente (proxy ARP) a solicitudes ARP por hosts remotos conocidos, evitando tener que inundar (flood) esas solicitudes ARP por todo el fabric — esto se conoce como supresión de ARP.

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: Why does VXLAN encapsulate frames over UDP rather than a different transport?

options.A: UDP allows the use of source port hashing (based on the inner frame) to enable effective load balancing/ECMP across the IP underlay for VXLAN traffic
options.B: UDP encrypts the payload automatically, which VXLAN needs for security
options.C: UDP is required because VXLAN cannot run over IP networks otherwise
options.D: UDP provides connection-oriented, guaranteed delivery required for VXLAN

questions.explanation_es: VXLAN usa UDP principalmente porque permite variar el puerto UDP de origen (calculado con un hash del contenido de la trama interna), lo cual habilita un buen balanceo de carga/ECMP a través del underlay IP, ya que los switches intermedios pueden usar ese puerto como parte del hash de balanceo. UDP no es garantizado ni orientado a conexión.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: In a traditional 3-tier campus design, what is the primary role of the distribution layer?

options.A: To serve as the high-speed backbone that interconnects distribution blocks, applying little to no policy in order to maximize throughput
options.B: To directly connect end-user devices and wireless access points, providing the physical port density needed at the network edge
options.C: To function only as a Layer 1 repeater with no Layer 2 switching or Layer 3 routing capability of its own
options.D: To aggregate access-layer uplinks, apply policy/QoS, and provide Layer 2/Layer 3 boundary and routing between access blocks

questions.explanation_es: La capa de distribución agrega los enlaces de la capa de acceso, aplica políticas (QoS, ACLs) y suele ser el límite entre Capa 2 y Capa 3, enrutando entre los distintos bloques de acceso. No conecta directamente a los usuarios finales (eso es la capa de acceso).

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: What is a key characteristic of a 'collapsed core' (2-tier) design compared to a 3-tier design?

options.A: It is a design pattern that is only supported in Cisco SD-Access fabric deployments and cannot be used in traditional campus networks
options.B: It removes the access layer entirely, connecting end-user devices straight into the combined distribution/core switches
options.C: It adds a dedicated core layer on top of distribution and access, increasing the total device count compared to a 3-tier design
options.D: The distribution and core layer functions are combined into a single layer, typically suited for smaller networks

questions.explanation_es: En un diseño de 2 capas (collapsed core), las funciones de distribución y núcleo se combinan en una sola capa, reduciendo la cantidad de dispositivos y siendo apropiado para redes más pequeñas donde una capa de núcleo dedicada no se justifica.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Stateful Switchover (SSO) between redundant supervisors/route processors?

options.A: To synchronize control-plane state between an active and standby supervisor so that a switchover happens without a full reboot or routing protocol reconvergence
options.B: To load-balance traffic dynamically across multiple redundant links between the same pair of devices
options.C: To provide default gateway redundancy for end hosts, allowing a backup router to take over IP addressing duties if the primary fails
options.D: To encrypt control-plane traffic exchanged between the active and standby supervisors for confidentiality

questions.explanation_es: SSO sincroniza el estado del plano de control entre un supervisor activo y uno standby, de forma que si ocurre un failover, el standby puede tomar el control sin necesidad de un reinicio completo ni una reconvergencia total de los protocolos de enrutamiento.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: What problem do First Hop Redundancy Protocols (FHRPs) like HSRP and VRRP primarily solve?

options.A: They replace the need for Spanning Tree Protocol by eliminating Layer 2 loops directly at the gateway
options.B: They are used exclusively to provide redundant paths across WAN links between remote sites
options.C: They provide redundancy for DNS servers, allowing clients to resolve names even if one DNS server fails
options.D: They provide redundancy for the default gateway seen by end hosts, so a single router/switch failure doesn't disrupt host connectivity

questions.explanation_es: Los FHRP (HSRP, VRRP, GLBP) resuelven el problema de que los hosts finales normalmente apuntan a un único gateway por defecto; si ese router falla, los FHRP permiten que otro router asuma esa IP virtual de forma transparente para el host.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: In Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, what is the primary role of the vSmart controller?

options.A: It is the control-plane element that distributes routing/policy information to edge routers using OMP (Overlay Management Protocol)
options.B: It is used exclusively to stage and push firmware upgrades to WAN Edge routers
options.C: It acts as the data-plane element deployed at each branch, forwarding all customer traffic across IPsec tunnels
options.D: It provides only DHCP and NTP services to branch sites, with no role in routing or policy

questions.explanation_es: El vSmart controller es el elemento de plano de control en SD-WAN; distribuye información de enrutamiento y políticas a los edge routers mediante OMP (Overlay Management Protocol), de forma similar a un route reflector de BGP pero para el overlay SD-WAN.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: What is the role of the vBond orchestrator in a Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN deployment?

options.A: It stores all historical telemetry and performance data collected from every WAN Edge router
options.B: It performs deep packet inspection and application-layer firewalling on user data-plane traffic
options.C: It replaces vManage as the source of configuration templates pushed to WAN Edge routers
options.D: It handles initial authentication and orchestration, helping edge devices and controllers discover each other, including NAT traversal

questions.explanation_es: vBond actúa como el orquestador: autentica inicialmente a los dispositivos y controladores, y facilita que se descubran entre sí (incluyendo asistencia para atravesar NAT), permitiendo que se establezcan las conexiones seguras hacia vSmart y vManage.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: Which is a commonly cited benefit of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN over traditional WAN architectures?

options.A: Transport independence — the ability to use any combination of MPLS, broadband internet, or LTE while centrally managing policy and routing over that mixed transport
options.B: It requires no controllers of any kind, since policy is configured manually on each WAN Edge device
options.C: It eliminates the need for any dedicated WAN transport at all, relying solely on the LAN for site-to-site connectivity
options.D: It guarantees zero packet loss regardless of the underlying transport's quality or congestion level

questions.explanation_es: Uno de los beneficios centrales de SD-WAN es la independencia de transporte: se puede combinar MPLS, banda ancha, LTE, etc., mientras la política de enrutamiento y seguridad se gestiona de forma centralizada por encima de esos transportes.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: Which of the following is a legitimate limitation to consider when adopting an SD-WAN solution?

options.A: It introduces additional architectural complexity (controllers, overlay management) that must be designed, secured, and operated correctly
options.B: SD-WAN eliminates all need for staff to understand routing concepts, since the overlay configures itself
options.C: SD-WAN cannot support any encryption of traffic between sites, leaving all data exposed over the transport
options.D: SD-WAN cannot be used with more than one branch site, limiting it to single-site deployments only

questions.explanation_es: Aunque SD-WAN aporta flexibilidad, también introduce complejidad adicional: hay que diseñar, asegurar y operar controladores (vManage, vSmart, vBond) y el overlay, lo cual requiere nuevas habilidades y consideraciones operativas frente al WAN tradicional.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: In Cisco SD-Access, what is the role of the Fabric Control Plane node?

options.A: It is only used for onboarding wireless clients, with no role for wired endpoints in the fabric
options.B: It replaces the need for a fabric border node, handling all external connectivity to outside networks itself
options.C: It maintains a host-tracking database (based on LISP) that maps endpoint identity to its current location (RLOC) in the fabric
options.D: It forwards all data-plane traffic exclusively, performing VXLAN encapsulation for every packet entering the fabric

questions.explanation_es: El Fabric Control Plane node en SD-Access mantiene una base de datos de host-tracking basada en LISP, que mapea la identidad del endpoint (EID) a su ubicación actual en el fabric (RLOC), permitiendo movilidad transparente.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What is the function of a Fabric Border Node in an SD-Access deployment?

options.A: It replaces the need for external DHCP servers by assigning IP addresses to endpoints directly
options.B: It is responsible exclusively for encrypting all fabric traffic between edge nodes using MACsec
options.C: It only manages wireless SSIDs and radio configuration for access points connected within the fabric
options.D: It connects the SD-Access fabric to networks outside the fabric, such as the traditional network, WAN, or Internet

questions.explanation_es: El Fabric Border Node es el punto de conexión entre el fabric de SD-Access y redes externas al fabric (red tradicional, WAN, Internet), actuando como el límite de entrada/salida de tráfico hacia y desde el fabric.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: When integrating a traditional (non-fabric) network segment with an SD-Access fabric, what device typically provides route leaking between the fabric's VRFs and the traditional network's global routing table?

options.A: A wireless LAN controller, since it already maintains a mapping of client locations across the fabric
options.B: The Fabric Edge Node exclusively, since it already handles VXLAN encapsulation for connected endpoints
options.C: A Fusion Router, which handles route leaking/exchange between fabric VRFs and external networks
options.D: The DHCP server, since it already assigns IP addressing across every VRF in the fabric

questions.explanation_es: Un Fusion Router (router de fusión) es el dispositivo típicamente usado para hacer route leaking entre las VRFs del fabric SD-Access y la tabla de enrutamiento global de la red tradicional externa, ya que el Border Node normalmente no filtra/combina VRFs por sí solo.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: According to Cisco QoS best-practice marking recommendations, which DSCP value should be used to mark voice bearer (RTP) traffic?

options.A: CS3 (Class Selector 3)
options.B: EF (Expedited Forwarding)
options.C: CS5 (Class Selector 5)
options.D: AF31 (Assured Forwarding 31)

questions.explanation_es: El tráfico de voz (RTP, portador de la llamada) se marca con EF (Expedited Forwarding, DSCP 46), que está diseñado para tráfico sensible a latencia y jitter con baja tolerancia a pérdida. AF31/CS3 se usan típicamente para señalización de llamadas, no para el audio en sí.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What is the difference between traffic classification and traffic marking in a QoS policy?

options.A: Classification identifies/categorizes traffic based on criteria (ACL, DSCP, application); marking sets a field (like DSCP or CoS) in the packet/frame to reflect that classification for downstream devices
options.B: Classification only applies to Layer 2 frames using the CoS field, while marking only applies to Layer 3 packets
options.C: Marking always happens before classification, since the DSCP value is what determines which class a packet belongs to
options.D: They are the same operation with different names — classification and marking both refer to setting the DSCP or CoS field

questions.explanation_es: La clasificación identifica y agrupa el tráfico según algún criterio (ACL, aplicación, etc.); el marcado (marking) es la acción de escribir un valor (como DSCP o CoS) en el paquete/trama para que dispositivos posteriores en la red puedan aplicar tratamiento diferenciado sin tener que reclasificar.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: What is the key architectural difference between a Type 1 and a Type 2 hypervisor?

options.A: Type 2 hypervisors cannot run more than one VM
options.B: A Type 1 hypervisor runs directly on the physical hardware (bare-metal); a Type 2 hypervisor runs as an application on top of a host operating system
options.C: They are functionally identical, differing only in licensing
options.D: A Type 1 hypervisor requires a host OS, while Type 2 does not

questions.explanation_es: Un hipervisor Tipo 1 (bare-metal, ej. ESXi, Hyper-V) corre directamente sobre el hardware físico sin un sistema operativo host intermedio; un hipervisor Tipo 2 (ej. VMware Workstation, VirtualBox) corre como una aplicación encima de un sistema operativo host existente.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: Why are Type 1 hypervisors generally preferred for production data center/server virtualization over Type 2?

options.A: Type 1 hypervisors typically offer better performance and lower overhead since they interact directly with hardware without a host OS layer in between
options.B: Type 1 hypervisors are always free while Type 2 are not
options.C: Type 2 hypervisors cannot support networking at all
options.D: Type 1 hypervisors cannot support more than one guest OS

questions.explanation_es: Al eliminar la capa de sistema operativo host intermedio, los hipervisores Tipo 1 suelen ofrecer mejor rendimiento y menor overhead, por lo que son la opción preferida en entornos de producción de centros de datos.

questions.name: VMs / FT / DRS
questions.question: What is the primary benefit of VM encapsulation (a VM being represented as a set of files)?

options.A: It requires the VM to always run on the same physical host
options.B: It prevents the VM from ever being backed up
options.C: It eliminates the need for a hypervisor
options.D: It allows a VM to be easily copied, moved, or migrated between hosts, since its entire state is contained in portable files

questions.explanation_es: Como una VM se encapsula como un conjunto de archivos (disco virtual, configuración, memoria), resulta fácil copiarla, moverla o migrarla entre hosts distintos, ya que todo su estado está contenido de forma portable.

questions.name: VMs / FT / DRS
questions.question: What does live migration (e.g., VMware vMotion) allow an administrator to do?

options.A: Disable all networking on a VM
options.B: Convert a VM into a physical server
options.C: Move a running VM from one physical host to another with minimal to no downtime, without powering it off
options.D: Permanently delete a VM's virtual disk

questions.explanation_es: La migración en vivo (como vMotion) permite mover una VM en ejecución de un host físico a otro con downtime mínimo o nulo, sin apagarla, típicamente para balanceo de carga entre hosts o mantenimiento de hardware.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a VRF (Virtual Routing and Forwarding) instance on a router?

options.A: To create multiple independent routing tables on a single device, allowing overlapping IP address spaces and traffic isolation between different routing domains
options.B: To encrypt all traffic on the router
options.C: To replace the need for VLANs on switches
options.D: To provide Layer 2 switching only

questions.explanation_es: Una VRF crea múltiples tablas de enrutamiento independientes en un mismo dispositivo, permitiendo que direcciones IP se solapen entre distintas VRFs y aislando el tráfico de enrutamiento entre dominios lógicos distintos, útil en escenarios multi-tenant o de segmentación.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: What is a key characteristic of GRE (Generic Routing Encapsulation) tunneling?

options.A: GRE only works with IPv4 payloads, never IPv6
options.B: GRE requires IPsec to function at all
options.C: GRE always encrypts the payload using AES
options.D: GRE encapsulates a wide variety of protocols but provides no encryption or authentication by itself

questions.explanation_es: GRE (protocolo IP 47) encapsula una amplia variedad de protocolos de capa 3 dentro de un túnel IP, pero por sí mismo no ofrece cifrado ni autenticación; por eso frecuentemente se combina con IPsec (GRE over IPsec) cuando se necesita seguridad.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the IPsec protocols AH and ESP?

options.A: AH is used for tunnel mode only; ESP is used for transport mode only
options.B: AH (Authentication Header) provides authentication and integrity but no encryption; ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload) provides both encryption and authentication/integrity
options.C: AH provides encryption only; ESP provides authentication only
options.D: AH and ESP are functionally identical and interchangeable

questions.explanation_es: AH (Authentication Header) provee autenticación e integridad, pero NO cifrado. ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload) provee tanto cifrado como autenticación/integridad, por lo que ESP es la opción más usada cuando se requiere confidencialidad de los datos.

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: In LISP (Locator/ID Separation Protocol), what is the function of the ETR (Egress Tunnel Router)?

options.A: It decapsulates LISP-encapsulated traffic destined for its local site and registers its EID-to-RLOC mappings with the Map-Server
options.B: It replaces the Map-Resolver
options.C: It is only used to originate encapsulated traffic, never to receive it
options.D: It performs no role in the LISP control plane

questions.explanation_es: El ETR (Egress Tunnel Router) recibe y desencapsula el tráfico LISP destinado a su sitio local, y es responsable de registrar sus mapeos EID-a-RLOC ante el Map-Server, para que otros sitios puedan resolver cómo alcanzarlo.

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: What is the role of the Map-Resolver in a LISP architecture?

options.A: It stores end-user application data
options.B: It is identical in function to an ETR
options.C: It receives map requests from ITRs and forwards them to the appropriate Map-Server to resolve an EID-to-RLOC mapping
options.D: It performs the actual data-plane encapsulation of traffic

questions.explanation_es: El Map-Resolver recibe las solicitudes de mapeo (Map-Request) de los ITRs y las reenvía al Map-Server correspondiente para resolver el mapeo EID-a-RLOC, funcionando como intermediario en el plano de control de LISP.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'native VLAN' on an 802.1Q trunk link?

options.A: The native VLAN is where all trunk control-plane traffic like DTP and CDP is encrypted
options.B: The native VLAN can never be VLAN 1
options.C: Native VLAN only applies to RSTP domains
options.D: Frames belonging to the native VLAN are sent untagged across the trunk, while all other VLANs are tagged

questions.explanation_es: En un trunk 802.1Q, las tramas de la VLAN nativa se envían sin etiqueta (untagged), mientras que las demás VLANs se envían con su etiqueta 802.1Q correspondiente. Es importante que ambos extremos del trunk configuren la misma VLAN nativa para evitar problemas de seguridad/conectividad.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: What does DTP (Dynamic Trunking Protocol) do on a Cisco switch link?

options.A: It replaces the need for 802.1Q tagging
options.B: It dynamically negotiates whether a link becomes a trunk or an access port between two Cisco switches
options.C: It assigns IP addresses to trunk interfaces
options.D: It is used only for routing protocol negotiation

questions.explanation_es: DTP es un protocolo propietario de Cisco que negocia dinámicamente si un enlace entre dos switches Cisco se convierte en trunk o en puerto de acceso, según los modos configurados (auto, desirable, on, nonegotiate) en cada extremo.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes LACP from PAgP as EtherChannel negotiation protocols?

options.A: They are functionally and operationally identical with no meaningful difference
options.B: LACP cannot support more than 2 active links
options.C: LACP is an IEEE standard (802.3ad/802.1AX) usable in multivendor environments; PAgP is a Cisco-proprietary protocol usable only between Cisco devices
options.D: PAgP is the IEEE standard, and LACP is Cisco-proprietary

questions.explanation_es: LACP (Link Aggregation Control Protocol) es un estándar IEEE (802.3ad/802.1AX), por lo que se puede usar entre dispositivos de distintos fabricantes; PAgP (Port Aggregation Protocol) es propietario de Cisco y solo funciona entre dispositivos Cisco.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What determines how traffic is distributed across the links of an EtherChannel bundle?

options.A: EtherChannel does not support load balancing at all
options.B: A load-balancing hashing algorithm (e.g., based on source/destination MAC, IP, or port) selects which physical link a given flow uses
options.C: Traffic is always sent round-robin, one frame per link regardless of flow
options.D: Only the first configured link in the bundle is ever used

questions.explanation_es: El reparto de tráfico entre los enlaces físicos de un EtherChannel se determina mediante un algoritmo de hashing configurable (basado en MAC origen/destino, IP origen/destino, puerto, etc.), que asigna cada flujo a un enlace físico específico del bundle, manteniendo el orden de las tramas dentro de un mismo flujo.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What is the key difference in purpose between Root Guard and BPDU Guard?

options.A: Root Guard prevents a port from becoming the root port/root bridge by blocking superior BPDUs, while BPDU Guard disables a port entirely (typically an edge/PortFast port) upon receiving any BPDU
options.B: Root Guard blocks all traffic on a port, not just BPDUs
options.C: BPDU Guard is used only on trunk ports, Root Guard only on access ports
options.D: They are functionally identical STP protection features

questions.explanation_es: Root Guard evita que un puerto se convierta en puerto raíz (y por lo tanto que un switch downstream se convierta en el root bridge) bloqueando BPDUs superiores; BPDU Guard, en cambio, deshabilita completamente el puerto (típicamente uno configurado como edge/PortFast) al recibir cualquier BPDU, asumiendo que en ese puerto no debería haber otro switch conectado.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: In RSTP (802.1w), what is the purpose of the 'alternate' port role?

options.A: It provides a backup path to the root bridge via a different segment, ready to quickly transition to forwarding if the current root port fails
options.B: It is a port that is always forwarding traffic simultaneously with the root port
options.C: It only exists in legacy 802.1D STP, not RSTP
options.D: It refers to a port connected to an end host

questions.explanation_es: El rol de puerto 'alternate' en RSTP representa un camino de respaldo hacia el root bridge, a través de un switch/segmento distinto, listo para pasar rápidamente a forwarding si el puerto raíz actual falla, permitiendo la convergencia rápida característica de RSTP.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: In EIGRP's DUAL algorithm, what is a 'feasible successor'?

options.A: The only route that can ever be installed in the routing table
options.B: A route learned exclusively via redistribution
options.C: A route that always has a higher metric than the successor
options.D: A backup route to a destination that is guaranteed to be loop-free, kept in the topology table as a ready alternative if the successor route fails

questions.explanation_es: Un feasible successor en EIGRP es una ruta de respaldo hacia un destino que está garantizada matemáticamente (por el criterio de factibilidad) a estar libre de loops; se mantiene en la tabla de topología como alternativa lista para usarse instantáneamente si la ruta successor (la instalada) falla, sin necesidad de recálculo.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: How does OSPF primarily calculate its cost metric for a link, by default on Cisco devices?

options.A: Based on a reference bandwidth divided by the interface bandwidth (cost = reference-bandwidth / interface-bandwidth)
options.B: Based purely on hop count, like RIP
options.C: Based on the interface's MTU only
options.D: Based on a random value assigned at boot

questions.explanation_es: Por defecto, OSPF calcula el costo de un enlace como el resultado de dividir un ancho de banda de referencia (reference bandwidth, 100 Mbps por defecto) entre el ancho de banda configurado en la interfaz; enlaces más rápidos obtienen un costo menor. RIP, en cambio, usa conteo de saltos.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: In OSPFv3, what addressing is used to form neighbor adjacencies between routers?

options.A: Global unicast IPv6 addresses only
options.B: Link-local IPv6 addresses, even though the topology/prefix information exchanged can include global addresses
options.C: IPv4 addresses, since OSPFv3 is backward compatible
options.D: MAC addresses exclusively

questions.explanation_es: En OSPFv3, las adyacencias de vecinos se forman usando direcciones IPv6 link-local, independientemente de que la información de topología y prefijos intercambiada en los LSAs pueda incluir direcciones IPv6 globales. Esta es una diferencia clave respecto a OSPFv2.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What is the defining characteristic of an OSPF 'totally stubby' area?

options.A: It is identical to a standard stub area with no differences
options.B: It can only be used as the backbone area (Area 0)
options.C: It allows all LSA types without restriction
options.D: It blocks both external (Type 5) LSAs and inter-area (Type 3) summary LSAs, injecting only a default route into the area

questions.explanation_es: Un área totally stubby bloquea tanto las LSA externas (Tipo 5, de redistribución) como las LSA de resumen inter-área (Tipo 3), inyectando en su lugar solo una ruta por defecto hacia esas áreas/destinos externos, reduciendo aún más el tamaño de la tabla de enrutamiento comparado con un área stub normal.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: In the BGP best-path selection process, which attribute is evaluated first among these two: Weight or Local Preference?

options.A: Local Preference is always evaluated before Weight
options.B: They are evaluated simultaneously and tie-broken randomly
options.C: Weight is evaluated before Local Preference
options.D: Neither is used in the actual best-path algorithm

questions.explanation_es: En el algoritmo de selección de mejor ruta de BGP, Weight (un atributo propietario de Cisco, local al router) se evalúa antes que Local Preference. Weight nunca se anuncia a otros routers, mientras que Local Preference sí se comparte dentro del AS local.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: By default, what TTL value is used for eBGP peering between directly connected neighbors, and why does this matter?

options.A: TTL of 1, meaning the BGP packets are expected to arrive from a directly connected neighbor only one hop away; multihop eBGP requires explicitly enabling 'ebgp-multihop'
options.B: TTL is negotiated dynamically and cannot be fixed
options.C: TTL has no relevance to eBGP sessions
options.D: TTL of 255 always, regardless of topology

questions.explanation_es: Por defecto, eBGP usa un TTL de 1, asumiendo que el vecino está directamente conectado (un solo salto). Si se necesita establecer una sesión eBGP con un vecino que está a más de un salto de distancia, hay que configurar explícitamente 'ebgp-multihop' para aumentar el TTL permitido.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Policy-Based Routing (PBR)?

options.A: To provide encryption for routed traffic
options.B: To perform Layer 2 switching decisions
options.C: To forward traffic based on criteria other than just the destination IP address, such as source address, application, or packet size, overriding the normal routing table decision
options.D: To replace the routing table entirely with static routes

questions.explanation_es: PBR permite tomar decisiones de reenvío basadas en criterios distintos a la simple dirección IP de destino (por ejemplo, dirección de origen, tipo de aplicación, tamaño de paquete), anulando la decisión normal basada en la tabla de enrutamiento cuando coincide con la política definida.

questions.name: NTP/PTP
questions.question: What does the 'stratum' number represent in NTP (Network Time Protocol)?

options.A: The number of clients an NTP server can support
options.B: The physical location of the NTP server
options.C: The encryption strength used by the NTP session
options.D: The distance (in hops) from the reference clock source; stratum 0 devices are the reference clocks themselves, stratum 1 servers are directly connected to them, and the number increases with each additional hop

questions.explanation_es: El stratum en NTP indica la distancia jerárquica respecto a la fuente de reloj de referencia: stratum 0 son los relojes de referencia mismos (ej. GPS), stratum 1 son servidores directamente sincronizados a esos relojes, y el número aumenta a medida que se aleja de la fuente.

questions.name: NTP/PTP
questions.question: Why is PTP (Precision Time Protocol, IEEE 1588) generally preferred over NTP in environments requiring sub-microsecond time accuracy?

options.A: NTP is always more precise than PTP
options.B: PTP and NTP provide identical accuracy in all cases
options.C: PTP is designed to achieve much higher time synchronization precision (sub-microsecond) than NTP, which typically achieves millisecond-level accuracy over a network
options.D: PTP works only over serial links, never Ethernet

questions.explanation_es: PTP está diseñado para lograr una precisión de sincronización de tiempo mucho mayor (a nivel de sub-microsegundos) que NTP, que típicamente logra precisión a nivel de milisegundos sobre una red. Por eso PTP se usa en entornos que requieren sincronización extremadamente precisa, como telecomunicaciones o sistemas financieros.

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: How does PAT (Port Address Translation) allow multiple internal hosts to share a single public IP address?

options.A: It uses source port numbers to distinguish between the different internal sessions sharing the same translated public IP address
options.B: It assigns a different public IP to each internal host dynamically from a large pool
options.C: It requires each internal host to use a different VLAN
options.D: It encrypts each session to distinguish them

questions.explanation_es: PAT (también llamado NAT overload) traduce múltiples direcciones IP internas a una única IP pública, distinguiendo cada sesión mediante el número de puerto de origen, que se traduce a un puerto único en la tabla de traducción, permitiendo miles de sesiones simultáneas compartiendo una sola IP pública.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: In HSRP, what are the two primary states a router can be in for a given HSRP group (besides transitional states)?

options.A: Active and Standby
options.B: Master and Backup
options.C: Root and Alternate
options.D: Primary and Secondary

questions.explanation_es: En HSRP, los dos estados principales de un router dentro de un grupo son Active (el que reenvía el tráfico para la IP virtual) y Standby (el que está listo para asumir el rol activo si el actual falla). Nota: VRRP usa la terminología 'Master' y 'Backup' en lugar de Active/Standby.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes VRRP from HSRP?

options.A: They are identical protocols with different names only
options.B: VRRP is an IEEE/IETF open standard (RFC 3768/5798) usable across vendors, while HSRP is Cisco-proprietary; also, VRRP can use a router's own real interface IP as the virtual IP if desired
options.C: VRRP cannot support preemption, while HSRP can
options.D: HSRP is the open standard and VRRP is Cisco-proprietary

questions.explanation_es: VRRP es un estándar abierto (RFC 3768/5798) utilizable entre distintos fabricantes, mientras que HSRP es propietario de Cisco. Además, VRRP permite que la IP virtual coincida con la IP real de la interfaz de uno de los routers (el 'IP address owner'), algo que HSRP no contempla de la misma forma.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What is the purpose of the RPF (Reverse Path Forwarding) check in multicast routing?

options.A: It verifies that a multicast packet arrived on the interface that the unicast routing table would use to reach the source, preventing loops and duplicate delivery
options.B: It converts multicast traffic into unicast
options.C: It has no relation to loop prevention
options.D: It encrypts multicast traffic

questions.explanation_es: El chequeo RPF verifica que un paquete multicast llegó por la interfaz que, según la tabla de enrutamiento unicast, se usaría para alcanzar la fuente de ese tráfico. Si no coincide, el paquete se descarta, lo cual previene loops y entrega duplicada en árboles de distribución multicast.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What is the key difference between PIM Sparse Mode (PIM-SM) using shared trees and PIM Source-Specific Multicast (SSM)?

options.A: SSM always requires an RP, while PIM-SM never does
options.B: PIM-SM initially builds a shared tree through a Rendezvous Point (RP) and can later switch to a source tree; SSM requires the receiver to specify the exact source, building a source tree directly without needing an RP
options.C: PIM-SM only works with IPv6, and SSM only works with IPv4
options.D: They are functionally identical

questions.explanation_es: PIM-SM construye inicialmente un árbol compartido a través de un Rendezvous Point (RP), pudiendo luego cambiar a un árbol de fuente (source tree, SPT) para optimizar la ruta. SSM (Source-Specific Multicast), en cambio, requiere que el receptor especifique explícitamente la fuente (S,G) y construye un árbol de fuente directamente, sin necesidad de un RP.

questions.name: Diagnóstico (debug/traceroute/ping/SNMP/syslog)
questions.question: What is the fundamental difference between an SNMP trap and an SNMP poll?

options.A: A poll is always sent by the device, and a trap is always requested by the manager
options.B: Traps can only carry interface counters, never other data
options.C: Traps and polls are the same mechanism with different names
options.D: A trap is sent proactively (unsolicited) by the managed device to the SNMP manager when an event occurs, while a poll is a request initiated by the manager to query the device for information

questions.explanation_es: Un trap SNMP es enviado proactivamente (sin haber sido solicitado) por el dispositivo gestionado hacia el gestor SNMP cuando ocurre un evento relevante; un poll, en cambio, es una consulta iniciada por el gestor que solicita información al dispositivo bajo demanda (típicamente vía GET).

questions.name: Diagnóstico (debug/traceroute/ping/SNMP/syslog)
questions.question: In Cisco syslog severity levels, which numeric level corresponds to 'critical' messages, and how does severity numbering generally work?

options.A: Severity levels only apply to SNMP, not syslog
options.B: All syslog messages have the same severity by default
options.C: Level 7 is critical, and higher numbers mean more severe
options.D: Level 2 is critical; lower numeric severity levels indicate more severe conditions (0=emergency being the most severe, 7=debugging being the least severe)

questions.explanation_es: En syslog de Cisco, los niveles de severidad van de 0 a 7, donde los números más bajos indican condiciones más severas: 0=emergency, 1=alert, 2=critical, 3=error, 4=warning, 5=notification, 6=informational, 7=debugging. El nivel 'critical' corresponde al número 2.

questions.name: Flexible NetFlow
questions.question: In Flexible NetFlow, what defines a 'flow record'?

options.A: It refers only to the destination for exported NetFlow data
options.B: A flow record defines the set of key fields (used to identify unique flows, such as source/destination IP and port) and non-key fields (collected data, such as byte/packet counts) that will be exported for each flow
options.C: It is a fixed, non-configurable template that cannot vary between deployments
options.D: It is simply the physical interface where NetFlow is enabled

questions.explanation_es: Un flow record en Flexible NetFlow define qué campos clave (key fields, que identifican de forma única un flujo, como IP/puerto origen-destino) y qué campos no clave (non-key fields, datos recopilados como contadores de bytes/paquetes) se exportarán para cada flujo. A diferencia de NetFlow tradicional, en Flexible NetFlow estos campos son totalmente configurables.

questions.name: Flexible NetFlow
questions.question: In a Flexible NetFlow configuration, what is the role of the 'exporter' component, as distinct from the 'monitor'?

options.A: Only the monitor is required; the exporter is optional in all cases
options.B: The exporter defines which fields are collected, and the monitor defines the destination
options.C: The exporter defines the destination (IP address, port, transport) where the collected flow data will be sent, while the monitor ties together the record, the exporter, and the interface where flow data is collected
options.D: The exporter and monitor are the same configuration object under different names

questions.explanation_es: El exporter define el destino (dirección IP, puerto, transporte) hacia donde se enviarán los datos de flujo recopilados; el monitor (flow monitor) es el que une el flow record (qué campos recopilar), el exporter (a dónde enviar) y se aplica a la interfaz donde se recopilan los datos.

questions.name: SPAN/RSPAN/ERSPAN
questions.question: What is the key difference between RSPAN and ERSPAN?

options.A: RSPAN mirrors traffic across multiple switches within the same Layer 2 domain using a dedicated VLAN; ERSPAN encapsulates mirrored traffic in GRE, allowing it to be routed across a Layer 3 network to a remote destination
options.B: RSPAN can cross Layer 3 boundaries, while ERSPAN cannot
options.C: They are functionally identical, differing only in the vendor that supports them
options.D: ERSPAN can only be used on a single local switch
