questions.explanation_es: RSPAN permite reflejar tráfico entre switches dentro del mismo dominio de Capa 2, usando una VLAN dedicada para transportar el tráfico espejado. ERSPAN encapsula el tráfico espejado en GRE, lo que le permite ser enrutado a través de una red Capa 3 hacia un destino remoto, superando la limitación de RSPAN de quedar confinado a un dominio L2.

questions.name: IP SLA
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Cisco IP SLA (Service Level Agreement)?

options.A: To replace the need for routing protocols
options.B: To provide QoS marking for all traffic on an interface
options.C: To actively generate synthetic traffic and measure network performance metrics such as latency, jitter, and packet loss between two points
options.D: To perform Layer 2 loop detection

questions.explanation_es: IP SLA genera tráfico sintético de prueba de forma activa entre dos puntos de la red y mide métricas de desempeño como latencia, jitter y pérdida de paquetes, permitiendo monitorear proactivamente el estado del servicio (por ejemplo, para validar SLAs o disparar acciones como cambios de ruta ante degradación).

questions.name: Catalyst Center
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the core role of Cisco Catalyst Center (formerly DNA Center) in an enterprise network?

options.A: It provides centralized, intent-based network configuration, monitoring (Assurance), and management, including AI-powered workflows for troubleshooting and optimization
options.B: It is exclusively a wireless-only management platform
options.C: It functions only as a syslog collector with no configuration capabilities
options.D: It is a Layer 2 switch used only in the access layer

questions.explanation_es: Catalyst Center centraliza la configuración de red basada en intención (intent-based), el monitoreo y aseguramiento (Assurance) de la red, y añade flujos de trabajo potenciados por IA para troubleshooting y optimización proactiva, tanto para infraestructura cableada como inalámbrica.

questions.name: NETCONF/RESTCONF
questions.question: Which of these are core NETCONF operations used to retrieve and modify device configuration?

options.A: SELECT and UPDATE, borrowed from SQL
options.B: NETCONF has no defined operations; it is purely a transport
options.C: <get-config> to retrieve configuration data and <edit-config> to modify configuration data within a target datastore
options.D: Only HTTP GET and POST, since NETCONF is HTTP-based

questions.explanation_es: NETCONF define operaciones RPC específicas como <get-config> para recuperar la configuración de un datastore, y <edit-config> para modificarla; estas operaciones se intercambian en mensajes XML sobre una sesión persistente, típicamente sobre SSH, a diferencia de RESTCONF que usa verbos HTTP.

questions.name: Líneas y autenticación local
questions.question: What is the difference between configuring a simple line password on a VTY line versus configuring local username-based authentication?

options.A: Local username authentication cannot be combined with AAA
options.B: They provide identical security and auditability
options.C: Line passwords are always more secure than username-based authentication
options.D: A line password authenticates anyone who knows the shared password with no per-user accountability; local username authentication requires individual credentials, providing per-user identification and accountability

questions.explanation_es: Una simple contraseña de línea (line password) autentica a cualquiera que la conozca, sin distinguir quién se conectó (sin accountability individual). La autenticación con usuario local (username/password) requiere credenciales individuales por persona, lo que permite identificar y auditar quién accedió, y es la base para integrarse luego con AAA.

questions.name: AAA (TACACS+/RADIUS)
questions.question: How does TACACS+ differ from RADIUS regarding the AAA functions of Authentication and Authorization?

options.A: Neither protocol distinguishes Authentication from Authorization
options.B: TACACS+ separates Authentication and Authorization into distinct processes/packets, offering more granular control; RADIUS combines Authentication and Authorization into a single process
options.C: RADIUS separates Authentication and Authorization, while TACACS+ combines them
options.D: TACACS+ does not support Authorization at all

questions.explanation_es: TACACS+ separa la Autenticación y la Autorización en procesos/paquetes distintos, lo que permite un control más granular (por ejemplo, autorizar comandos específicos de forma independiente); RADIUS, en cambio, combina Autenticación y Autorización en un único proceso, lo que ofrece menos granularidad.

questions.name: AAA (TACACS+/RADIUS)
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a difference in what TACACS+ and RADIUS encrypt in their protocol exchanges?

options.A: TACACS+ encrypts the entire body of the packet, while RADIUS only encrypts the password field in the access-request packet
options.B: Both encrypt the entire packet identically
options.C: RADIUS encrypts the entire packet, while TACACS+ only encrypts the password
options.D: Neither protocol encrypts anything by default

questions.explanation_es: TACACS+ cifra todo el cuerpo del paquete en la comunicación entre el cliente AAA y el servidor, mientras que RADIUS por defecto solo cifra el campo de contraseña en el paquete Access-Request, dejando el resto de la información (como el nombre de usuario) sin cifrar.

questions.name: ACLs
questions.question: What is the primary functional difference between a standard ACL and an extended ACL on a Cisco device?

options.A: Extended ACLs can only be applied outbound, never inbound
options.B: A standard ACL can only match based on source IP address; an extended ACL can match based on source/destination IP, protocol, and port numbers, allowing much more granular filtering
options.C: They are functionally identical, differing only in numbering range
options.D: A standard ACL can filter based on Layer 4 ports, while extended cannot

questions.explanation_es: Una ACL estándar solo puede filtrar tráfico basándose en la dirección IP de origen. Una ACL extendida puede filtrar basándose en dirección IP de origen y destino, protocolo (TCP/UDP/ICMP, etc.) y números de puerto, permitiendo un filtrado mucho más granular.

questions.name: CoPP
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Control Plane Policing (CoPP)?

options.A: To replace the need for any ACLs on the device
options.B: To encrypt all traffic passing through the device's data plane
options.C: To provide QoS marking exclusively for user data traffic, not control-plane traffic
options.D: To protect the device's control-plane CPU from being overwhelmed by excessive or malicious traffic destined to the route processor, by rate-limiting or filtering that traffic

questions.explanation_es: CoPP protege la CPU del plano de control del dispositivo de ser sobrecargada por tráfico excesivo o malicioso destinado al procesador de rutas (por ejemplo, tráfico de gestión, protocolos de enrutamiento, o intentos de ataque), aplicando límites de tasa (rate-limiting) o filtrado específicamente a ese tráfico dirigido al propio dispositivo.

questions.name: Seguridad de REST API
questions.question: Why is token-based authentication (such as OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens) generally preferred over sending a username/password on every REST API call?

options.A: Tokens can be scoped, time-limited, and revoked independently of the user's actual credentials, reducing the exposure of long-term credentials on every request
options.B: Token-based authentication removes the need for HTTPS
options.C: Tokens never expire, unlike passwords
options.D: Sending username/password on every call is always more secure than tokens

questions.explanation_es: Los tokens (como los bearer tokens de OAuth 2.0) pueden tener alcance limitado (scopes), expirar después de cierto tiempo, y ser revocados de forma independiente, reduciendo la exposición de las credenciales de largo plazo del usuario en cada solicitud, a diferencia de enviar usuario/contraseña repetidamente.

questions.name: Threat defense
questions.question: What does the security principle of 'defense in depth' refer to?

options.A: Relying on a single, very strong security control to protect the entire network
options.B: Implementing multiple, layered security controls (e.g., firewalls, IPS, endpoint security, segmentation) so that if one layer fails, others still provide protection
options.C: A specific Cisco product name
options.D: Only securing the network perimeter and trusting everything inside

questions.explanation_es: Defense in depth (defensa en profundidad) es el principio de implementar múltiples capas de controles de seguridad (firewalls, IPS, seguridad de endpoint, segmentación, etc.) de forma que si una capa falla o es comprometida, las demás sigan brindando protección, en lugar de depender de un único control.

questions.name: Seguridad de endpoint (NAC/ISE)
questions.question: What is the purpose of posture assessment in a NAC (Network Access Control) solution like Cisco ISE?

options.A: It only assigns an IP address to the endpoint
options.B: It is used exclusively for wireless SSID broadcast
options.C: It evaluates whether an endpoint meets defined security compliance criteria (e.g., updated antivirus, patches) before or after granting network access, potentially placing non-compliant devices into a restricted/remediation network
options.D: It replaces the need for 802.1X authentication

questions.explanation_es: El posture assessment evalúa si un endpoint cumple con criterios de seguridad definidos (antivirus actualizado, parches, cifrado de disco, etc.) antes o después de otorgar acceso a la red, y puede colocar a los dispositivos no conformes en una red restringida o de remediación hasta que cumplan los requisitos.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: What capability distinguishes a Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW) from a traditional stateful firewall?

options.A: Traditional stateful firewalls already include full application-layer inspection
options.B: NGFWs cannot perform stateful inspection at all
options.C: An NGFW adds application awareness/visibility, integrated intrusion prevention (IPS), and user identity-based policy, going beyond simple port/protocol-based stateful filtering
options.D: An NGFW can only filter based on source/destination IP, just like a traditional firewall

questions.explanation_es: Un NGFW agrega capacidades de conciencia de aplicación (identificar qué app genera el tráfico más allá del puerto), IPS integrado, y políticas basadas en identidad de usuario, yendo más allá del simple filtrado stateful basado en puerto/protocolo que ofrece un firewall tradicional.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: In Python, what is the key structural difference between a 'list' and a 'dictionary' (dict)?

options.A: They are functionally identical data structures with different syntax
options.B: A dictionary cannot store more than one value
options.C: A list is an ordered collection of items accessed by numeric index; a dictionary is a collection of key-value pairs accessed by a unique key
options.D: A list can only store strings, while a dictionary can store any type

questions.explanation_es: Una 'list' en Python es una colección ordenada de elementos, accesibles por índice numérico (ej. lista[0]); un 'dict' es una colección de pares clave-valor, accesibles por una clave única (ej. diccionario['nombre']), similar conceptualmente a un objeto JSON.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: Which of the following is a valid, well-formed JSON object?

options.A: {"name": "router1", "status": "up"}
options.B: {name: router1, status: up}
options.C: (name=router1, status=up)
options.D: {'name': 'router1', 'status': 'up'}

questions.explanation_es: JSON exige que las claves y los valores de tipo string usen comillas dobles (") exclusivamente; las comillas simples (') no son válidas en JSON estándar, aunque sí lo sean en Python. La opción con comillas dobles es la única realmente bien formada.

questions.name: Códigos de respuesta REST API
questions.question: When interpreting an API response, what does an HTTP status code in the 5xx range generally indicate, as opposed to a 4xx code?

options.A: 5xx codes always mean the request succeeded
options.B: 4xx and 5xx codes mean the same thing
options.C: 5xx codes are used only for successful redirects
options.D: A 5xx code indicates a server-side error (the server failed to fulfill a valid request), whereas a 4xx code indicates a client-side error (the request itself was invalid or unauthorized)

questions.explanation_es: Un código en el rango 5xx indica un error del lado del servidor (el servidor no pudo cumplir una solicitud que en principio era válida, ej. 500 Internal Server Error), mientras que un código 4xx indica un error del lado del cliente (la solicitud en sí era inválida, mal formada, o no autorizada, ej. 400, 401, 404).

questions.name: Códigos de respuesta REST API
questions.question: When an API call to Catalyst Center returns a 202 Accepted status with a taskId in the payload, what does this typically indicate?

options.A: 202 means the exact same thing as 200 OK with no practical difference
options.B: The taskId is used only for billing purposes
options.C: The request failed and must be resent immediately
options.D: The request was accepted for asynchronous processing, and the client should poll the task status endpoint using the returned taskId to check completion

questions.explanation_es: Un código 202 Accepted en Catalyst Center indica que la solicitud fue aceptada para procesamiento asíncrono (por ejemplo, una tarea de provisioning que toma tiempo); el cliente debe usar el taskId devuelto para consultar el endpoint de estado de tareas y verificar cuándo (y cómo) se completó la operación.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: Which EEM (Embedded Event Manager) event detector would you use to trigger an applet based on CPU utilization crossing a defined threshold?

options.A: event none, which never triggers automatically
options.B: event cli, matching a specific command entered by a user
options.C: event snmp, watching a specific OID
options.D: event cpu, which monitors CPU utilization against a configured threshold, or the equivalent resource-based event detector for that purpose

questions.explanation_es: Para disparar un applet EEM basado en el uso de CPU superando un umbral, se utiliza un detector de eventos orientado a recursos como 'event cpu' (o el detector de recursos correspondiente), que monitorea la utilización de CPU y dispara la acción configurada cuando se cruza el umbral definido. 'event cli' se usa para disparar en base a un comando ingresado, no en base a CPU.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: What is the key architectural difference between agent-based orchestration tools (like Chef or Puppet) and agentless tools (like Ansible)?

options.A: Agent-based tools require software installed and running on the managed node to communicate with the central server; agentless tools typically connect to managed nodes over standard protocols (like SSH) without requiring persistent installed software
options.B: Agentless tools always require more installed software than agent-based tools
options.C: They are functionally identical in terms of architecture
options.D: Agent-based tools cannot be used to manage network devices

questions.explanation_es: Las herramientas basadas en agente (como Chef o Puppet) requieren que un software (agente) esté instalado y corriendo en el nodo gestionado para comunicarse con el servidor central; las herramientas agentless (como Ansible) típicamente se conectan a los nodos gestionados usando protocolos estándar (como SSH) sin requerir la instalación de software persistente en el nodo.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: Which HTTP method is most appropriate for retrieving a resource's current state without modifying anything, mapping to the 'Read' operation in CRUD?

options.A: DELETE
options.B: PUT
options.C: GET
options.D: POST

questions.explanation_es: GET se usa para recuperar (leer) el estado actual de un recurso sin modificarlo, correspondiendo a la operación 'Read' en el modelo CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete). POST se usa típicamente para Create, PUT/PATCH para Update, y DELETE para Delete.

questions.name: Diseños de red
questions.question: In Cisco SD-Access, what is the primary purpose of the 'underlay' network?

options.A: To provide basic IP reachability between fabric nodes (routed access), over which the VXLAN overlay is built
options.B: To replace the need for any IP addressing scheme, since the fabric relies solely on MAC-based forwarding
options.C: To carry only wireless client traffic between access points and the wireless LAN controller
options.D: To provide the policy and segmentation function of the fabric using Scalable Group Tags

questions.explanation_es: El underlay en SD-Access es una red enrutada (routed access) que provee conectividad IP básica entre los nodos del fabric; sobre esta base se construye el overlay VXLAN que transporta el tráfico de los endpoints con segmentación (SGT) aplicada.

questions.name: Diseños de red
questions.question: What is a defining principle of cloud-based/cloud-managed network design (e.g., Meraki-style or Catalyst Center cloud management)?

options.A: Centralized management and monitoring delivered via a cloud/SaaS-based controller, reducing the need for on-premises management infrastructure
options.B: It eliminates the need for any local network hardware, since all switching happens inside the cloud provider's data center
options.C: It only applies to wireless networks, since wired switches cannot be managed through a cloud dashboard
options.D: All switching and routing decisions are made in the cloud on a per-packet basis, with no local forwarding intelligence

questions.explanation_es: El diseño de red gestionado por la nube centraliza la gestión, configuración y monitoreo a través de un controlador SaaS, reduciendo la necesidad de infraestructura de gestión local, aunque el reenvío de tráfico en sí sigue ocurriendo en los dispositivos locales, no en la nube.

questions.name: Diseños de red
questions.question: In a 3-tier campus design, what is the primary role of the core layer?

options.A: To directly connect end-user devices and provide Power over Ethernet for endpoints such as phones and access points
options.B: To apply detailed per-user QoS and security policy for every flow passing between distribution blocks
options.C: To perform DHCP relay for every VLAN in the campus, forwarding broadcast requests to the DHCP server
options.D: To provide a high-speed backbone that switches/routes traffic between distribution blocks, with minimal policy enforcement to maximize throughput and low latency

questions.explanation_es: La capa de núcleo (core) provee un backbone de alta velocidad que conmuta/enruta tráfico entre los distintos bloques de distribución, aplicando el mínimo de políticas posible para maximizar el throughput y minimizar la latencia; la aplicación detallada de políticas ocurre normalmente en distribución o acceso.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: How does GLBP (Gateway Load Balancing Protocol) differ from HSRP/VRRP in terms of gateway utilization?

options.A: GLBP is simply Cisco's proprietary name for VRRP, providing no functional difference from it
options.B: GLBP does not support any form of redundancy, requiring a separate FHRP to be configured alongside it
options.C: GLBP can only have one router forwarding traffic, exactly like HSRP
options.D: GLBP allows active load balancing across multiple routers simultaneously (multiple routers forward traffic at once), whereas HSRP/VRRP use only one active/master router at a time per group

questions.explanation_es: GLBP permite balanceo de carga activo entre múltiples routers simultáneamente (varios routers reenvían tráfico a la vez, cada uno respondiendo ARP con una MAC virtual distinta), a diferencia de HSRP/VRRP donde solo un router (activo/master) reenvía tráfico por grupo en un momento dado.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: What does 'preemption' mean in the context of FHRP (HSRP/VRRP/GLBP)?

options.A: It refers to encrypting the FHRP control messages (hellos) exchanged between routers in the group
options.B: It disables the FHRP group permanently once a failover has occurred, requiring manual re-enablement
options.C: It prevents any router from ever becoming active again after a failure
options.D: It allows a router with higher priority to reclaim the active/master role once it comes back online, even if another router is currently active

questions.explanation_es: La preferencia (preemption) permite que un router con mayor prioridad reclame el rol activo/master una vez que vuelve a estar disponible, incluso si otro router de menor prioridad ya asumió ese rol durante la falla. Es importante notar que en HSRP está deshabilitada por defecto, mientras que en VRRP está habilitada por defecto.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: What is the difference between 'N+1' redundancy and 'active/active' redundancy as general high-availability concepts?

options.A: N+1 always means at least two extra spare units per active unit
options.B: Active/active means only one unit is ever operational at a time
options.C: They are the same redundancy concept, just described using different vendor-specific terminology
options.D: N+1 means one extra standby unit is ready to take over if an active unit fails; active/active means multiple units are simultaneously handling traffic, often providing both redundancy and load distribution

questions.explanation_es: N+1 se refiere a tener una unidad adicional (standby) de respaldo lista para asumir el trabajo si una unidad activa falla; active/active significa que múltiples unidades manejan tráfico simultáneamente, aportando tanto redundancia como distribución de carga (a diferencia del modelo activo/standby tradicional).

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: What is the primary function of Cisco vManage in an SD-WAN deployment?

options.A: It is the only device responsible for actually forwarding customer data-plane traffic
options.B: It replaces vSmart as the control-plane element, distributing routing and policy information via OMP
options.C: It performs NAT traversal and initial orchestration exclusively
options.D: It provides a centralized dashboard for configuration, monitoring, and management of the entire SD-WAN fabric

questions.explanation_es: vManage es el elemento de gestión centralizada en Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN: provee el dashboard para configurar, monitorear y administrar toda la solución (plantillas, políticas, visibilidad), aunque el plano de control lo maneja vSmart y el de datos los WAN Edge routers.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: What information does OMP (Overlay Management Protocol) distribute in a Cisco SD-WAN fabric?

options.A: Only NTP time synchronization data used to keep WAN Edge clocks aligned
options.B: Only DNS records used to resolve internal hostnames across the SD-WAN fabric
options.C: Only firmware update packages staged for distribution to WAN Edge routers
options.D: Routes, TLOC (transport location) information, security keys, and policy information between vSmart controllers and WAN Edge routers

questions.explanation_es: OMP es el protocolo de plano de control de SD-WAN (similar en concepto a BGP) que distribuye rutas, información de ubicación de transporte (TLOC), claves de seguridad para IPsec, y políticas entre los controladores vSmart y los routers WAN Edge.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: What is the role of a WAN Edge router in Cisco SD-WAN?

options.A: It is the data-plane element deployed at branch/campus/data center sites that actually forwards user traffic across the SD-WAN fabric, establishing secure IPsec tunnels to other WAN Edges
options.B: It only performs control-plane functions, never forwarding actual traffic
options.C: It is used only to track and report software licensing compliance back to Cisco
options.D: It is identical in function to vManage, providing the centralized dashboard for configuration and monitoring

questions.explanation_es: El WAN Edge router es el elemento de plano de datos, desplegado en las sedes (branch, campus, data center), que efectivamente reenvía el tráfico de usuario a través del fabric SD-WAN, estableciendo túneles IPsec seguros hacia otros WAN Edges según la política definida.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: How does centralized policy management in SD-WAN typically benefit segmentation across many branch sites?

options.A: It requires each branch to have its own unique, manually configured policy with no central coordination
options.B: It only works for a single branch site at a time, requiring separate policy management per site
options.C: It removes the need for any segmentation at all, since every site shares one flat, unsegmented network
options.D: It allows consistent segmentation and security policy to be defined once and pushed to all sites, instead of manually configuring each branch router individually

questions.explanation_es: Con SD-WAN, la política de segmentación y seguridad se puede definir de forma centralizada una sola vez y distribuirse automáticamente a todas las sedes, en lugar de configurar manualmente cada router de sucursal, mejorando consistencia y reduciendo errores operativos.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: What is a common benefit of enabling Direct Internet Access (DIA) at branch sites in an SD-WAN design?

options.A: It disables all security inspection at the branch, sending traffic to the internet completely unfiltered
options.B: It forces all internet traffic to be backhauled through a single central hub, increasing latency
options.C: It is only relevant for MPLS-only deployments, since broadband circuits already provide direct internet access
options.D: It allows branch sites to send internet-bound traffic (e.g., SaaS applications) directly to the internet rather than backhauling it through a central data center, reducing latency and WAN bandwidth usage

questions.explanation_es: DIA permite que el tráfico destinado a Internet (por ejemplo, aplicaciones SaaS) salga directamente desde la sucursal en lugar de hacer backhaul a través de un data center central, reduciendo la latencia percibida por el usuario y liberando ancho de banda del WAN core.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: Why is high availability design for SD-WAN controllers (vManage, vSmart, vBond) an important consideration rather than an afterthought?

options.A: Because only vManage requires redundancy, while vSmart and vBond can safely run as single points of failure
options.B: Because these controllers are central to configuration, control-plane routing, and orchestration; if not deployed redundantly, their failure can significantly impact the ability to manage or even maintain the overlay fabric
options.C: Because SD-WAN controllers cannot be made redundant under any circumstances, regardless of deployment size
options.D: Because controllers have no operational impact if they fail, since WAN Edges continue forwarding traffic fully independently

questions.explanation_es: Al centralizar funciones críticas de configuración (vManage), plano de control (vSmart) y orquestación (vBond), la falla de estos controladores sin diseño de alta disponibilidad puede afectar significativamente la capacidad de gestionar la red o incluso mantener el overlay, por lo que suelen desplegarse en clústeres redundantes.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What is the role of a Fabric Edge Node in Cisco SD-Access?

options.A: It is the node where endpoints (users, devices) connect, performing VXLAN encapsulation/decapsulation of their traffic into the fabric
options.B: It is the exclusive point of connection to external networks
options.C: It only manages the Map-Server database that tracks EID-to-RLOC mappings for the fabric
options.D: It replaces the need for any control plane node, maintaining its own host-tracking database independently

questions.explanation_es: El Fabric Edge Node es donde se conectan los endpoints (equivalente a un switch de acceso en el fabric); es responsable de encapsular/desencapsular el tráfico de esos endpoints en VXLAN para transportarlo dentro del fabric hacia su destino.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What data-plane encapsulation does Cisco SD-Access use to carry traffic between fabric nodes?

options.A: VXLAN, which also carries the SGT information needed for policy enforcement
options.B: MPLS labels exclusively, requiring every fabric node to run a full MPLS label distribution protocol
options.C: GRE without any VLAN or segmentation information
options.D: Plain 802.1Q VLAN tagging only, with no additional overlay encapsulation between fabric nodes

questions.explanation_es: SD-Access utiliza VXLAN como encapsulación del plano de datos entre nodos del fabric; el encabezado VXLAN también transporta la SGT (Security Group Tag), permitiendo aplicar políticas de segmentación de forma consistente a través del fabric.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: In SD-Access, what does a 'fabric-enabled' Wireless LAN Controller (WLC) primarily allow?

options.A: The elimination of the need for any access points, since clients associate directly with the fabric edge switch
options.B: Wireless traffic to be integrated directly into the fabric overlay, with the WLC participating in fabric control-plane registration for wireless clients
options.C: Wireless traffic to bypass all fabric policy entirely, since APs forward it directly to the upstream router
options.D: Wired traffic to be tunneled over wireless links whenever a wired port is unavailable

questions.explanation_es: Un WLC fabric-enabled integra el tráfico inalámbrico directamente en el overlay del fabric SD-Access, registrando los clientes inalámbricos en el plano de control (LISP) igual que los clientes cableados, permitiendo aplicar la misma política de segmentación de forma unificada.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: When extending an existing VLAN from a traditional network segment into an SD-Access fabric, which consideration is important regarding the fabric's approach to Layer 2/Layer 3 boundaries?

options.A: SD-Access typically uses a routed (Layer 3) access model with VXLAN overlay per virtual network, so extending traditional VLANs requires mapping them carefully into fabric virtual networks/IP pools rather than simply trunking VLANs end-to-end as in a traditional design
options.B: VLANs cannot exist in any form within an SD-Access fabric, since all segmentation is done purely through Scalable Group Tags
options.C: There is no need to consider Layer 2/Layer 3 boundaries in SD-Access, since the fabric flattens the network into one broadcast domain
options.D: SD-Access uses the exact same VLAN trunking model as a traditional campus, with 802.1Q trunks carried unmodified between all switches

questions.explanation_es: A diferencia de una red tradicional donde una VLAN puede extenderse por trunking Capa 2 entre switches, SD-Access usa típicamente un modelo de acceso enrutado (Capa 3) con overlay VXLAN por red virtual; extender conectividad hacia/desde una VLAN tradicional requiere mapearla cuidadosamente a una red virtual del fabric (y su pool IP asociado), no simplemente extender el trunk como en el diseño tradicional.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What is the difference between congestion management (queuing) and congestion avoidance mechanisms in QoS?

options.A: Congestion management only works on wireless interfaces, since wired interfaces never experience congestion
options.B: They are identical mechanisms, both dropping packets proactively before a queue fills to prevent congestion
options.C: Congestion avoidance only applies to UDP traffic, since TCP already handles its own flow control
options.D: Congestion management (e.g., queuing algorithms like LLQ, CBWFQ) determines how traffic is scheduled/prioritized when congestion occurs; congestion avoidance (e.g., WRED) proactively drops packets before a queue fully fills, to prevent TCP global synchronization and worse congestion

questions.explanation_es: La gestión de congestión (colas como LLQ, CBWFQ) determina cómo se prioriza y programa el tráfico cuando ya hay congestión; la prevención de congestión (como WRED) descarta paquetes de forma proactiva antes de que una cola se llene completamente, evitando la sincronización global de TCP y una congestión aún peor.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What is the difference between traffic policing and traffic shaping?

options.A: Policing can only be applied outbound, and shaping only inbound
options.B: Policing typically drops (or re-marks) traffic that exceeds a defined rate immediately, with no buffering; shaping buffers/delays excess traffic to smooth it out and conform to the rate over time, rather than dropping it outright
options.C: Shaping always drops traffic immediately, while policing buffers it
options.D: They are functionally identical QoS mechanisms that both buffer excess traffic to smooth out bursts

questions.explanation_es: El policing (limitación) típicamente descarta o re-marca de inmediato el tráfico que excede la tasa configurada, sin buffer. El shaping (moldeado) almacena en buffer el tráfico excedente para suavizarlo y ajustarlo a la tasa a lo largo del tiempo, en lugar de descartarlo directamente, resultando en menos pérdida de paquetes a costa de mayor latencia/jitter potencial.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What is the concept of a 'trust boundary' in a QoS design?

options.A: The maximum bandwidth allowed for any given interface before QoS policies begin dropping traffic
options.B: A boundary that only exists in wireless networks, since wired switches always trust incoming markings by default
options.C: A physical firewall placed between two QoS domains to inspect and re-mark traffic crossing between them
options.D: The point in the network (often the access-layer edge, at the endpoint or switch port) where the network decides whether to trust the QoS markings applied by the connected device, or to re-classify/re-mark them itself

questions.explanation_es: El trust boundary es el punto de la red (a menudo el borde de la capa de acceso, en el switch o incluso el propio endpoint si es confiable, como un teléfono IP) donde se decide si confiar en las marcas de QoS que trae el tráfico entrante, o si reclasificarlas/remarcarlas, para evitar que dispositivos no confiables marquen su propio tráfico con alta prioridad indebidamente.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: What does a hypervisor fundamentally do with a physical server's hardware resources?

options.A: It virtualizes the physical CPU, memory, storage, and network resources, partitioning them into multiple isolated virtual machines that share the same underlying hardware
options.B: It only virtualizes storage, never CPU or memory
options.C: It removes the need for any physical hardware
options.D: It physically duplicates the hardware for each VM

questions.explanation_es: El hipervisor virtualiza los recursos físicos (CPU, memoria, almacenamiento, red) de un servidor, particionándolos en múltiples máquinas virtuales aisladas entre sí que comparten el mismo hardware subyacente, permitiendo consolidar múltiples cargas de trabajo en menos servidores físicos.

questions.name: VMs / FT / DRS
questions.question: What is the purpose of Fault Tolerance (FT) technology in a virtualized environment, as distinct from simple live migration (vMotion)?

options.A: FT keeps a live secondary copy of a VM running in lockstep on a different host, so if the primary host fails, the secondary instantly takes over with zero downtime and no loss of state
options.B: FT is identical to vMotion, just with a different name
options.C: FT eliminates the need for shared storage
options.D: FT only protects against application-level crashes, not host hardware failures

questions.explanation_es: Fault Tolerance mantiene una copia secundaria de la VM ejecutándose en paralelo (en lockstep) en otro host físico; si el host primario falla, la copia secundaria asume el control de forma instantánea, sin downtime ni pérdida de estado, a diferencia de vMotion que mueve la VM de forma planificada con una breve interrupción.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: What is 'VRF-lite' and how does it differ from a full MPLS VPN deployment using VRFs?

options.A: VRF-lite can only be used on a single interface, never across multiple devices
options.B: VRF-lite implements multiple VRFs on a router without using MPLS labels to carry VRF information across links; instead, it typically relies on separate physical/sub-interfaces per VRF between hops
options.C: VRF-lite requires MPLS labels exactly like a full VPN deployment
options.D: There is no meaningful difference between VRF-lite and MPLS VPN VRFs

questions.explanation_es: VRF-lite implementa múltiples VRFs en un router sin usar etiquetas MPLS para transportar la identificación de VRF entre saltos; en su lugar, típicamente se usan interfaces o subinterfaces separadas por VRF entre dispositivos adyacentes, siendo una solución más simple que una VPN MPLS completa, adecuada para segmentación en redes más pequeñas.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: What is a key benefit of using VRFs for multi-tenancy on a single physical router?

options.A: VRFs eliminate the need for any IP addressing plan
options.B: Multiple tenants (customers or departments) can share the same physical device while maintaining fully isolated routing tables, even with overlapping IP address ranges
options.C: VRFs require each tenant to use a completely separate physical router
options.D: VRFs can only support a single tenant per device

questions.explanation_es: Las VRFs permiten que múltiples inquilinos (tenants) compartan el mismo router físico manteniendo tablas de enrutamiento completamente aisladas entre sí, incluso pudiendo usar rangos de direcciones IP solapados entre distintos tenants, sin necesidad de un router físico dedicado por cliente.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: What is the key difference between IPsec tunnel mode and IPsec transport mode?

options.A: Tunnel mode encrypts the entire original IP packet (including its header) and adds a new outer IP header; transport mode encrypts only the payload, preserving the original IP header
options.B: Tunnel mode can only be used with AH, never with ESP
options.C: Transport mode encrypts the entire packet including the header; tunnel mode only encrypts the payload
options.D: They are functionally identical modes with different names

questions.explanation_es: El modo túnel de IPsec cifra el paquete IP original completo (incluyendo su encabezado) y le agrega un nuevo encabezado IP externo, siendo típico entre gateways/routers. El modo transporte cifra solo el payload, preservando el encabezado IP original, siendo más común en comunicaciones extremo a extremo entre dos hosts.

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: What is the core conceptual separation that LISP introduces compared to traditional IP addressing?

options.A: LISP separates 'identity' (EID — who/what the endpoint is) from 'location' (RLOC — where in the network topology it currently is), allowing mobility without renumbering
options.B: LISP only applies to Layer 2 MAC addresses, not IP
options.C: LISP eliminates the need for any IP addressing at all
options.D: LISP merges identity and location into a single unified address with no separation

questions.explanation_es: LISP introduce la separación conceptual entre identidad (EID — Endpoint Identifier, quién/qué es el endpoint) y ubicación (RLOC — Routing Locator, dónde está actualmente en la topología de red), permitiendo que un endpoint se mueva de ubicación sin necesidad de renumerar su dirección IP, lo cual es la base también usada por SD-Access.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: How many bits does the VLAN ID field occupy in an 802.1Q tag, and what is the resulting range of usable VLAN IDs?

options.A: 4 bits, allowing only 16 VLANs
options.B: 16 bits, allowing over 65,000 VLANs
options.C: 12 bits, allowing VLAN IDs from 0-4095, with 1-4094 typically usable (0 and 4095 reserved)
options.D: 8 bits, allowing only 256 VLANs

questions.explanation_es: El campo VLAN ID en la etiqueta 802.1Q ocupa 12 bits, lo que permite valores de 0 a 4095; en la práctica, los IDs 1 a 4094 son los usables para configuración normal (0 y 4095 están reservados para propósitos especiales).

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: What happens to a frame received untagged on an 802.1Q trunk port, assuming default configuration?

options.A: It is automatically dropped as invalid
options.B: It is treated as belonging to VLAN 0 always
options.C: It is treated as belonging to the native VLAN configured on that trunk
options.D: It causes the trunk to shut down

questions.explanation_es: Por comportamiento estándar de 802.1Q, una trama recibida sin etiqueta en un puerto trunk se considera perteneciente a la VLAN nativa configurada en ese trunk. Por eso es crítico que la VLAN nativa coincida en ambos extremos del enlace.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: Which mitigation is commonly recommended to reduce the risk of VLAN hopping attacks via double-tagging or DTP manipulation?

options.A: VLAN hopping cannot be mitigated in any way
options.B: Enable DTP auto-negotiation on every port to simplify configuration
options.C: Use VLAN 1 as the native VLAN on all trunks for consistency
options.D: Explicitly disable DTP negotiation on trunk/access ports (set them statically) and avoid using VLAN 1 as the native VLAN or for management traffic

questions.explanation_es: Para reducir el riesgo de ataques de VLAN hopping (por doble etiquetado o manipulación de DTP), se recomienda deshabilitar la negociación dinámica de DTP (configurando explícitamente trunk o access según corresponda) y evitar usar VLAN 1 como VLAN nativa o para tráfico de gestión, entre otras buenas prácticas de hardening.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: What does the PCP (Priority Code Point) field within an 802.1Q tag represent?

options.A: An encryption key used to protect the frame
options.B: The VLAN ID of the frame
options.C: A 3-bit field used to convey Layer 2 QoS priority (commonly referred to as CoS), allowing switches to prioritize frames based on this marking
options.D: The source MAC address of the sender

questions.explanation_es: El campo PCP (Priority Code Point), comúnmente conocido como CoS (Class of Service), es un campo de 3 bits dentro de la etiqueta 802.1Q que se usa para transmitir prioridad de QoS a nivel de Capa 2, permitiendo que los switches prioricen tramas según este valor.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: For an EtherChannel bundle to form correctly between two switches, what must generally match across the member links?

options.A: Nothing needs to match; any combination of speeds and duplex settings works
options.B: Only the port numbers need to be identical on both switches
options.C: Key parameters such as speed, duplex, trunk mode/allowed VLANs (if trunked), and native VLAN must be consistent across all member ports on both sides
options.D: Only the physical cable length needs to match

questions.explanation_es: Para que un EtherChannel se forme correctamente, los puertos miembros deben tener parámetros consistentes entre sí y entre ambos extremos: velocidad, duplex, y si es trunk, el modo trunk, las VLANs permitidas y la VLAN nativa deben coincidir; de lo contrario el bundle puede no formarse o comportarse de forma inconsistente.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: How many active links does a standard Cisco EtherChannel bundle typically support (without special stacking technology)?

options.A: Only 1 link, since EtherChannel is meant for single-link redundancy only
options.B: Up to 16 active links always
options.C: Only 2 links maximum
options.D: Up to 8 active links

questions.explanation_es: Un EtherChannel estándar en Cisco soporta típicamente hasta 8 enlaces activos en el bundle (con posibilidad de enlaces adicionales en modo standby usando LACP en algunas plataformas), permitiendo agregación de ancho de banda y redundancia.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What risk arises if one side of a link is configured as an EtherChannel bundle while the other side treats the links as individual (non-bundled) switchports?

options.A: Only performance is reduced, with no risk of loops
options.B: The link will always work correctly with no issues
options.C: It can create a Layer 2 loop, since the non-bundled side may forward the same broadcast/multicast frame out multiple individual links that the bundled side sees as a single logical link, confusing STP and potentially causing a broadcast storm
options.D: The mismatch is automatically detected and corrected by DTP

questions.explanation_es: Un desajuste de EtherChannel (un lado con el bundle configurado y el otro tratando los enlaces como puertos individuales) puede generar un loop de Capa 2, ya que el lado no-bundled puede reenviar la misma trama de broadcast/multicast por múltiples enlaces individuales que el lado bundled interpreta como un solo enlace lógico, confundiendo a STP y potencialmente causando una tormenta de broadcast.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What problem does MST (Multiple Spanning Tree) solve compared to running PVST+ (Per-VLAN Spanning Tree) with hundreds of VLANs?

options.A: MST requires running a completely separate spanning tree for every single VLAN, just like PVST+
options.B: MST eliminates the need for any spanning tree protocol at all
options.C: MST can only be used with a single VLAN
options.D: MST maps multiple VLANs to a smaller number of spanning-tree instances, reducing the CPU/control-plane overhead of running a separate STP instance per VLAN

questions.explanation_es: MST permite mapear múltiples VLANs a un número reducido de instancias de spanning tree (en lugar de una instancia por VLAN como en PVST+), reduciendo significativamente la carga de CPU y de control-plane en switches con cientos de VLANs, manteniendo la posibilidad de tener topologías distintas por grupo de VLANs si es necesario.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: Why is BPDU Guard commonly enabled together with PortFast on access ports?

options.A: They are never used together in practice
options.B: BPDU Guard is required for PortFast to function at all
options.C: PortFast and BPDU Guard perform the exact same function and are redundant together
options.D: PortFast skips the normal STP listening/learning states for fast connectivity on end-host ports, but this creates risk if a switch is accidentally connected there; BPDU Guard protects against that by shutting down the port if a BPDU is received

questions.explanation_es: PortFast salta los estados normales de listening/learning de STP para dar conectividad rápida en puertos de host final, pero esto es riesgoso si por error se conecta un switch en ese puerto (podría causar loops). BPDU Guard complementa a PortFast apagando el puerto automáticamente si llega a recibir una BPDU, protegiendo contra esa conexión indebida.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: How does RSTP (802.1w) convergence time generally compare to legacy 802.1D STP?

options.A: RSTP converges significantly faster (often sub-second, using mechanisms like proposal/agreement), whereas legacy 802.1D STP can take 30-50 seconds to converge through its listening/learning states
options.B: RSTP and 802.1D have identical convergence times in all cases
options.C: 802.1D always converges faster than RSTP
options.D: RSTP requires manual intervention to converge, unlike 802.1D

questions.explanation_es: RSTP converge de forma mucho más rápida que el STP clásico 802.1D (a menudo en menos de un segundo, gracias a mecanismos como el intercambio de propuesta/acuerdo entre switches vecinos), mientras que 802.1D puede tardar entre 30 y 50 segundos en converger al pasar por sus estados de listening y learning con temporizadores fijos.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What does Loop Guard protect against in an STP topology?

options.A: It is functionally identical to BPDU Guard
options.B: It prevents a non-designated port (root or alternate) from erroneously transitioning to the forwarding/designated state due to a unidirectional link failure where BPDUs simply stop arriving
options.C: It only applies to trunk ports carrying VLAN 1
options.D: It prevents any port from ever becoming the root port

questions.explanation_es: Loop Guard protege contra la situación en la que un puerto root o alternate deja de recibir BPDUs (por ejemplo, por una falla unidireccional del enlace) y, al no recibirlas, erróneamente asumiría que puede pasar a estado forwarding/designado, lo cual podría crear un loop. Loop Guard mantiene el puerto en un estado bloqueado (loop-inconsistent) hasta que vuelvan a recibirse BPDUs normalmente.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: By default, which two metrics does EIGRP's composite metric calculation primarily use (in default K-value configuration)?

options.A: Only reliability
options.B: Bandwidth and delay
options.C: Hop count and MTU only
options.D: Only hop count, exactly like RIP

questions.explanation_es: Por defecto (con los valores K estándar), la métrica compuesta de EIGRP se calcula principalmente usando el ancho de banda mínimo del camino y la suma de los retardos (delay) de las interfaces atravesadas; otros factores (carga, confiabilidad) están disponibles pero no se usan por defecto en la fórmula estándar.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What is the difference between an OSPF Type 1 (Router LSA) and a Type 2 (Network LSA)?

options.A: A Router LSA is only used in totally stubby areas
options.B: They are the exact same LSA type with different numbers
options.C: A Network LSA describes external routes redistributed into OSPF
options.D: A Router LSA describes a router's own links and their costs within an area; a Network LSA is originated by the DR on a multi-access segment and describes all routers attached to that segment

questions.explanation_es: La LSA Tipo 1 (Router LSA) es originada por cada router y describe sus propios enlaces y costos dentro de un área; la LSA Tipo 2 (Network LSA) es originada por el DR (Designated Router) en un segmento de acceso múltiple y describe todos los routers conectados a ese segmento, sirviendo para representar la topología de la red multiacceso de forma más eficiente.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What does the EIGRP 'variance' command allow?

options.A: It is used to change the EIGRP autonomous system number
options.B: It only affects equal-cost paths, having no effect on unequal-cost ones
options.C: Unequal-cost load balancing across multiple paths, as long as the alternate paths' metric is within the configured variance multiple of the best metric and they are feasible successors
options.D: It disables load balancing entirely

questions.explanation_es: El comando 'variance' en EIGRP permite balanceo de carga de costo desigual (unequal-cost load balancing): rutas alternativas cuyo métrica esté dentro de un múltiplo configurado (variance) de la mejor métrica, y que además sean feasible successors (garantizando ausencia de loops), pueden usarse simultáneamente para distribuir tráfico junto con la ruta principal.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Why is DR/BDR election necessary on an OSPF multi-access (broadcast) network segment, but not on a point-to-point link?

options.A: On a multi-access segment, without a DR every router would form full adjacencies with every other router, causing an excessive number of adjacencies and LSA flooding; the DR/BDR reduces this by centralizing adjacency formation and LSA distribution
options.B: DR/BDR election is required on every OSPF network type, including point-to-point links, with no exceptions
options.C: DR/BDR election is only relevant for EIGRP, not OSPF
options.D: DR/BDR election exists purely for historical reasons and serves no functional purpose today

questions.explanation_es: En un segmento de acceso múltiple (broadcast), sin un DR cada router formaría adyacencias completas con todos los demás routers del segmento, generando una cantidad excesiva de adyacencias y de inundación de LSAs (n*(n-1)/2 adyacencias). El DR (y BDR como respaldo) centraliza la formación de adyacencias y la distribución de LSAs, reduciendo drásticamente esa sobrecarga. En enlaces punto a punto, al haber solo dos routers, no se necesita esta optimización.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What is the effect of configuring the 'passive-interface' command on an OSPF-enabled interface?

options.A: OSPF continues to advertise that interface's network in its LSAs, but stops sending/receiving OSPF hello packets on it, preventing neighbor adjacencies from forming over that interface
options.B: It completely removes the interface's network from being advertised by OSPF
options.C: It forces the interface to become the DR
options.D: It disables IP routing on that interface entirely

questions.explanation_es: 'Passive-interface' hace que OSPF deje de enviar/recibir paquetes hello por esa interfaz (evitando que se formen adyacencias de vecino ahí), pero la red de esa interfaz sigue siendo anunciada normalmente en las LSAs del router, útil por ejemplo en interfaces hacia LANs de usuarios donde no se espera un vecino OSPF.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: On which OSPF network types is DR/BDR election performed, versus not performed?

options.A: DR/BDR election occurs on all OSPF network types without exception
options.B: DR/BDR election only occurs on point-to-point networks
options.C: DR/BDR election never occurs under any OSPF network type
options.D: DR/BDR election occurs on broadcast and NBMA network types; it does NOT occur on point-to-point network types, since only two routers are involved

questions.explanation_es: La elección de DR/BDR ocurre en los tipos de red broadcast y NBMA (donde múltiples routers comparten el mismo segmento); en enlaces punto a punto no se realiza elección de DR/BDR, ya que al haber solo dos routers no existe la necesidad de optimizar la cantidad de adyacencias.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Where is OSPF route summarization typically configured for inter-area routes, versus for external (redistributed) routes?

options.A: Inter-area summarization is done on the ASBR, and external route summarization on the ABR — the reverse of the correct answer
options.B: Inter-area summarization is configured on the ABR (Area Border Router); summarization of external routes is configured on the ASBR (Autonomous System Boundary Router)
options.C: OSPF does not support any form of route summarization
options.D: Both types of summarization can only be configured on the backbone area 0 router directly, regardless of role

questions.explanation_es: La sumarización de rutas inter-área se configura en el ABR (Area Border Router), que resume las rutas de un área antes de anunciarlas hacia otras áreas. La sumarización de rutas externas (redistribuidas desde otro protocolo) se configura en el ASBR (Autonomous System Boundary Router), el punto donde esas rutas externas entran al dominio OSPF.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What does the OSPFv3 'address family' (AF) feature allow?

options.A: It removes IPv6 support from OSPFv3 entirely
options.B: It replaces the need for OSPFv2 entirely in dual-stack networks
options.C: It allows a single OSPFv3 process to support both IPv4 and IPv6 unicast topologies, maintaining separate address-family-specific routing information within one process
options.D: It is used only to configure authentication, with no relation to IPv4/IPv6 support

questions.explanation_es: La característica de Address Family (AF) en OSPFv3 permite que un único proceso OSPFv3 soporte topologías tanto IPv4 como IPv6 unicast, manteniendo información de enrutamiento separada por familia de direcciones dentro del mismo proceso, simplificando el despliegue dual-stack sin necesitar procesos OSPFv2 y OSPFv3 completamente independientes.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the BGP AS_PATH attribute?

options.A: It only records the next-hop IP address
options.B: It has no impact on best-path selection
options.C: It records the sequence of autonomous systems a route has traversed, used both for loop prevention (a router rejects a route containing its own AS) and as a factor in best-path selection (shorter AS_PATH generally preferred)
options.D: It is used exclusively for encryption of BGP updates

questions.explanation_es: El atributo AS_PATH registra la secuencia de sistemas autónomos que ha atravesado una ruta; se usa tanto para prevención de loops (un router rechaza una ruta que ya contiene su propio AS en el path) como para la selección de mejor ruta (un AS_PATH más corto es generalmente preferido, todo lo demás igual).

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: What is the default administrative distance difference between eBGP and iBGP routes on a Cisco router?

options.A: Administrative distance does not apply to BGP routes
options.B: Both eBGP and iBGP have the same administrative distance of 20
options.C: iBGP has a lower administrative distance than eBGP
options.D: eBGP has an administrative distance of 20, while iBGP has 200, making eBGP routes preferred over iBGP routes (and over most IGPs) by default when both are present for the same prefix

questions.explanation_es: Por defecto en Cisco, eBGP tiene una distancia administrativa de 20, mientras que iBGP tiene 200. Esto hace que, ante la misma prefijo aprendida por ambos, la ruta eBGP sea preferida (menor distancia administrativa = más confiable), y de hecho eBGP suele preferirse incluso sobre la mayoría de los IGPs internos.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: What is required for two routers to establish an eBGP neighbor relationship?

options.A: They require no configuration of AS numbers at all
options.B: They must always be in the same AS number
options.C: They must be configured with different autonomous system (AS) numbers, and typically be directly reachable (by default, one hop away unless multihop is configured)
options.D: They must use IGP metrics identical to each other

questions.explanation_es: Para establecer una relación de vecino eBGP, los routers deben pertenecer a AS distintos (a diferencia de iBGP, donde comparten el mismo AS), y típicamente deben ser alcanzables directamente (por defecto, a un salto de distancia, salvo que se configure ebgp-multihop para vecinos más alejados).

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: What is the purpose of BGP route aggregation (using the 'aggregate-address' command)?

options.A: To disable the advertisement of any routes
options.B: To encrypt BGP route advertisements
options.C: To split a single prefix into many smaller, more-specific prefixes automatically
options.D: To combine multiple more-specific prefixes into a single summarized prefix advertised to neighbors, reducing the size of the routing table advertised externally

questions.explanation_es: La agregación de rutas en BGP (comando 'aggregate-address') combina múltiples prefijos más específicos en un único prefijo resumido que se anuncia a los vecinos, reduciendo el tamaño de la tabla de rutas anunciada externamente y simplificando la topología vista por otros AS.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: In a Policy-Based Routing (PBR) route-map, which of the following is a typical 'match' criterion used to identify traffic for special routing treatment?

options.A: An access-list matching specific source addresses, or the packet length, among other criteria defined in the route-map
options.B: PBR route-maps only support matching on VLAN ID
options.C: PBR route-maps can only match on destination IP address, exactly like normal routing
options.D: PBR cannot use access-lists as match criteria

questions.explanation_es: En un route-map de PBR, un criterio de 'match' típico es una access-list que identifica el tráfico según su dirección de origen (u otros campos permitidos por la ACL), o también se puede hacer match por longitud de paquete, entre otros criterios; luego se define un 'set' para indicar el tratamiento especial (por ejemplo, el next-hop a usar) para ese tráfico coincidente.

questions.name: NTP/PTP
questions.question: Why is NTP authentication (e.g., using MD5 or SHA keys) recommended in a production network?

options.A: It encrypts all network traffic passing through the router, not just NTP
options.B: It has no security benefit and is purely cosmetic
options.C: It prevents a malicious or unauthorized source from injecting false time information, which could otherwise disrupt logging correlation, certificate validation, or other time-sensitive processes
options.D: It is required for NTP to function at all, even in a lab environment

questions.explanation_es: La autenticación NTP (usando claves MD5/SHA) previene que una fuente maliciosa o no autorizada inyecte información de tiempo falsa, lo cual podría afectar procesos sensibles al tiempo como la correlación de logs, validación de certificados digitales, o el registro correcto de eventos de seguridad.

questions.name: NTP/PTP
questions.question: What is the role of the 'grandmaster clock' in a PTP (Precision Time Protocol) domain?

options.A: It is the primary time reference source for the entire PTP domain, from which all other clocks in the hierarchy synchronize (directly or indirectly)
options.B: It performs no synchronization function in PTP
options.C: It refers to any client device receiving time from the network
options.D: It is a backup clock that only activates if all other clocks fail

questions.explanation_es: El grandmaster clock es la fuente de referencia de tiempo principal para todo el dominio PTP; todos los demás relojes en la jerarquía (boundary clocks, ordinary clocks) sincronizan su tiempo directa o indirectamente a partir de este reloj maestro, seleccionado mediante el Best Master Clock Algorithm (BMCA).

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: What is the difference between Static NAT and Dynamic NAT?

options.A: Static NAT can only be used with IPv6, and Dynamic NAT only with IPv4
options.B: They are functionally identical, differing only in configuration syntax
options.C: Static NAT creates a fixed, permanent one-to-one mapping between a specific inside local and inside global address; Dynamic NAT maps addresses from a pool on a first-come, first-served basis, without a fixed permanent mapping
options.D: Static NAT uses a pool of addresses, while Dynamic NAT always uses one fixed address

questions.explanation_es: Static NAT crea un mapeo fijo y permanente uno-a-uno entre una dirección local interna específica y una dirección global externa específica (útil por ejemplo para servidores que deben ser siempre alcanzables en la misma IP pública). Dynamic NAT, en cambio, asigna direcciones de un pool de forma dinámica, por orden de llegada, sin una asignación fija permanente.

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: In Cisco NAT terminology, what does 'inside local' refer to, as opposed to 'inside global'?

options.A: 'Inside global' refers to an external host's address, not an internal host's translated address
options.B: 'Inside local' is the address of an internal host as seen within the internal (private) network; 'inside global' is the translated address that represents that same internal host as seen from the external (public) network
options.C: 'Inside local' and 'inside global' refer to the exact same address with no distinction
options.D: These terms only apply to IPv6 NAT, not IPv4

questions.explanation_es: 'Inside local' es la dirección de un host interno tal como se ve dentro de la red privada (típicamente una IP privada RFC 1918); 'inside global' es la dirección traducida que representa a ese mismo host interno visto desde la red externa/pública, después de aplicar NAT.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: What is the standard virtual MAC address format used by HSRP (version 1) for a given group?

options.A: 0000.0C07.ACxx, where 'xx' represents the HSRP group number in hexadecimal
options.B: The real burned-in MAC address of the active router's physical interface, with no virtual MAC
options.C: A completely random MAC address generated at each failover
options.D: FFFF.FFFF.FFFF, the standard broadcast MAC

questions.explanation_es: HSRP versión 1 utiliza una dirección MAC virtual con el formato estándar 0000.0C07.ACxx, donde 'xx' representa el número de grupo HSRP en hexadecimal, permitiendo que los hosts sigan usando la misma MAC virtual sin importar cuál router físico esté actualmente activo.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: Regarding default preemption behavior, how do HSRP and VRRP differ?

options.A: Both protocols disable preemption by default with no differences
options.B: Neither protocol supports preemption at all
options.C: In VRRP, preemption is enabled by default; in HSRP, preemption is disabled by default and must be explicitly configured
options.D: In HSRP, preemption is enabled by default; in VRRP, it is disabled by default

questions.explanation_es: Una diferencia clave a tener presente: en VRRP la preferencia (preemption) está habilitada por defecto, mientras que en HSRP está deshabilitada por defecto y debe configurarse explícitamente si se desea que un router de mayor prioridad reclame el rol activo al recuperarse.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What is the purpose of IGMP (Internet Group Management Protocol)?

options.A: It is used to encrypt multicast traffic
options.B: It allows hosts to inform their local multicast router about which multicast groups they want to receive traffic for, enabling the router to determine where to forward multicast traffic on the local segment
options.C: It only operates between routers, never between a host and its local router
options.D: It replaces the need for PIM entirely across a routed network

questions.explanation_es: IGMP es el protocolo que permite a los hosts informar a su router multicast local a qué grupos multicast desean unirse (join), permitiendo que el router determine si debe reenviar tráfico multicast hacia ese segmento local. PIM, en cambio, se encarga del enrutamiento de multicast entre routers a través de la red.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What is the purpose of MSDP (Multicast Source Discovery Protocol)?

options.A: It is used exclusively for IGMP snooping on Layer 2 switches
options.B: It replaces PIM entirely as the multicast routing protocol
options.C: It is used only within a single PIM-SM domain, never between domains
options.D: It allows Rendezvous Points (RPs) in different PIM-SM domains to share information about active multicast sources, enabling inter-domain multicast source discovery

questions.explanation_es: MSDP permite que los Rendezvous Points (RP) de distintos dominios PIM-SM compartan información sobre fuentes multicast activas, habilitando el descubrimiento de fuentes multicast entre dominios independientes (inter-domain), algo que PIM-SM por sí solo no resuelve dentro de un único dominio.

questions.name: Diagnóstico (debug/traceroute/ping/SNMP/syslog)
questions.question: How does traceroute determine the sequence of hops (routers) along a path to a destination?

options.A: It sends probe packets with progressively increasing TTL values; each router that decrements the TTL to zero returns an ICMP 'Time Exceeded' message, revealing each hop along the path
options.B: It relies exclusively on SNMP queries to each router along the path
options.C: It requires manual configuration of every hop in advance
options.D: It uses a single packet with a fixed TTL of 255 for the entire path

questions.explanation_es: Traceroute envía paquetes de prueba con valores de TTL incrementales (empezando en 1); cada router que decrementa el TTL a cero descarta el paquete y responde con un mensaje ICMP 'Time Exceeded', revelando así, salto por salto, la ruta hacia el destino a medida que se incrementa el TTL en cada iteración.

questions.name: Diagnóstico (debug/traceroute/ping/SNMP/syslog)
questions.question: What underlying mechanism does the 'ping' utility use to test basic reachability to a destination?

options.A: TCP three-way handshake exclusively
options.B: ICMP Echo Request and Echo Reply messages
options.C: DNS queries
options.D: SNMP GET requests

questions.explanation_es: Ping utiliza mensajes ICMP Echo Request (enviados al destino) y Echo Reply (respondidos por el destino) para probar la conectividad básica y medir el tiempo de ida y vuelta (RTT), sin necesidad de establecer una sesión TCP.

questions.name: Flexible NetFlow
questions.question: How does NetFlow fundamentally differ from SPAN in terms of what data is collected?

options.A: They are functionally identical mechanisms
options.B: NetFlow collects summarized flow metadata/statistics (such as source/destination, byte and packet counts) rather than full packet copies; SPAN mirrors complete copies of the actual packets to an analysis destination
options.C: NetFlow copies every full packet, exactly like SPAN
options.D: SPAN only provides summarized statistics, never full packets

questions.explanation_es: NetFlow recopila metadatos y estadísticas resumidas de los flujos de tráfico (direcciones origen/destino, conteos de bytes/paquetes, etc.) sin capturar el contenido completo de cada paquete; SPAN, en cambio, refleja copias completas de los paquetes reales hacia un destino de análisis, siendo mucho más pesado en términos de ancho de banda pero ofreciendo visibilidad total del contenido.

questions.name: SPAN/RSPAN/ERSPAN
questions.question: What is a key limitation of local SPAN compared to RSPAN or ERSPAN?

options.A: Local SPAN can only mirror traffic to a destination port on the same physical switch where the source traffic is located
options.B: Local SPAN can mirror traffic to any destination across a routed WAN without any limitation
options.C: Local SPAN has no limitations compared to RSPAN or ERSPAN
options.D: Local SPAN requires GRE encapsulation, just like ERSPAN

questions.explanation_es: Una limitación clave de SPAN local es que solo puede reflejar tráfico hacia un puerto destino ubicado en el mismo switch físico donde está el tráfico origen; para monitorear tráfico y enviarlo a un destino en otro switch (dentro del mismo dominio L2) se necesita RSPAN, y para atravesar una red enrutada se necesita ERSPAN.

questions.name: SPAN/RSPAN/ERSPAN
questions.question: What constraint does RSPAN traffic have regarding how it can be transported across the network?

options.A: RSPAN traffic is automatically encrypted with IPsec
options.B: RSPAN traffic can be routed across any number of Layer 3 hops with no special encapsulation
options.C: RSPAN requires no dedicated VLAN and can use any regular data VLAN interchangeably
options.D: RSPAN traffic is carried over a dedicated RSPAN VLAN that must remain within a single Layer 2 (bridged) domain — it cannot be routed across a Layer 3 boundary, which is where ERSPAN would be needed instead

questions.explanation_es: El tráfico de RSPAN se transporta sobre una VLAN dedicada de RSPAN que debe permanecer dentro de un único dominio de Capa 2 (puenteado); no puede ser enrutado a través de un límite de Capa 3. Cuando se necesita llevar tráfico espejado a través de una red enrutada, se debe usar ERSPAN, que lo encapsula en GRE.

questions.name: IP SLA
questions.question: What is the purpose of an IP SLA 'responder' configured on the target device of a probe?

options.A: It converts the target device into an IP SLA source itself
options.B: It improves measurement accuracy (especially for jitter and latency) by timestamping the probe packets on the target device itself, rather than relying solely on round-trip estimates from the source
options.C: It is required only for ICMP-based operations, never for UDP-based ones
options.D: It blocks all IP SLA probes from reaching that device

questions.explanation_es: El IP SLA Responder, configurado en el dispositivo destino de la prueba, mejora la precisión de la medición (especialmente para jitter y latencia) al marcar con timestamp los paquetes de prueba en el propio dispositivo destino, en lugar de depender únicamente de estimaciones basadas en el tiempo de ida y vuelta medido solo desde el origen.

questions.name: IP SLA
questions.question: Which IP SLA operation type is commonly used to measure jitter, useful for validating voice/video quality over a path?

options.A: HTTP GET operation
options.B: FTP operation
options.C: DNS lookup operation
options.D: UDP jitter operation

questions.explanation_es: La operación de tipo UDP jitter de IP SLA está diseñada específicamente para medir jitter (variación en el retardo), latencia y pérdida de paquetes de forma similar al tráfico de voz/video real, siendo comúnmente usada para validar la calidad esperada de esos servicios sobre una ruta determinada antes o durante su despliegue.

questions.name: Catalyst Center
questions.question: How does Catalyst Center's Assurance capability typically obtain near-real-time visibility into network and client health, as opposed to relying solely on periodic polling?

options.A: By requiring the administrator to manually run 'show' commands on every device and paste the output in
options.B: By leveraging telemetry streaming from network devices and clients, in addition to traditional data collection methods, to provide more timely insight than polling alone
options.C: By disabling all monitoring capabilities on the managed devices
options.D: By relying exclusively on SNMP polling every 24 hours

questions.explanation_es: Catalyst Center Assurance aprovecha el streaming de telemetría desde los dispositivos de red y clientes (además de métodos de recolección más tradicionales), lo que permite una visibilidad mucho más cercana al tiempo real sobre la salud de la red y de los clientes, comparado con depender únicamente de polling periódico tradicional.

questions.name: Catalyst Center
questions.question: What does Cisco Catalyst Center's Plug and Play (PnP) capability enable?

options.A: It is used only for wireless access points, never for switches or routers
options.B: Zero-touch or near-zero-touch onboarding of new network devices, which automatically contact Catalyst Center upon first boot to receive their configuration and software image
options.C: It replaces the need for any IP addressing on new devices
options.D: It disables all automatic configuration, requiring fully manual setup for every new device

questions.explanation_es: Plug and Play (PnP) permite el onboarding de nuevos dispositivos de red con mínima o nula intervención manual: los dispositivos nuevos, al arrancar por primera vez, contactan automáticamente a Catalyst Center para recibir su configuración inicial e imagen de software correspondiente, simplificando el despliegue a gran escala.

questions.name: NETCONF/RESTCONF
questions.question: Over which transport and default port does NETCONF typically operate?

options.A: HTTP on port 80, exactly like RESTCONF
options.B: UDP on port 161, the same as SNMP
options.C: SSH, using the dedicated 'netconf' SSH subsystem, typically on TCP port 830
options.D: Plain unencrypted Telnet on port 23

questions.explanation_es: NETCONF típicamente opera sobre SSH, utilizando un subsistema SSH dedicado llamado 'netconf', normalmente en el puerto TCP 830, estableciendo una sesión persistente y segura para el intercambio de mensajes RPC en XML.

questions.name: NETCONF/RESTCONF
questions.question: Which of these correctly reflects an advantage of NETCONF's transaction-based approach using candidate/running datastores over RESTCONF's typical single-datastore model?

options.A: There is no meaningful difference between the two approaches
options.B: RESTCONF always supports a candidate/commit workflow identical to NETCONF
options.C: NETCONF's candidate datastore allows a set of changes to be staged and validated before an explicit commit is applied to the running configuration, supporting more controlled, transactional configuration changes
options.D: NETCONF has no concept of validating changes before applying them

questions.explanation_es: El uso del datastore 'candidate' en NETCONF permite preparar y validar un conjunto de cambios antes de aplicarlos formalmente (commit) a la configuración en ejecución (running), soportando un flujo de cambios más controlado y transaccional; RESTCONF, en cambio, opera típicamente de forma directa sobre un único datastore equivalente a running, sin ese paso intermedio de candidate/commit.

questions.name: Líneas y autenticación local
questions.question: What is the key security difference between the 'enable password' and 'enable secret' commands on a Cisco device?

options.A: Neither command has any impact on device security
options.B: 'enable secret' stores the password using a strong hash by default, while the older 'enable password' stores it in a much weaker, reversible/plaintext-like form; 'enable secret' should always be preferred
options.C: 'enable password' is always more secure than 'enable secret'
options.D: They are identical in security, differing only in command syntax

questions.explanation_es: 'enable secret' almacena la contraseña usando un hash fuerte por defecto, mientras que el comando más antiguo 'enable password' la almacena de una forma mucho más débil (tipo 7, fácilmente reversible), por lo que 'enable secret' siempre debe preferirse; si ambos están configurados, 'enable secret' tiene prioridad.

questions.name: Líneas y autenticación local
questions.question: Why is SSH generally preferred over Telnet for remote device management access?

options.A: SSH encrypts the entire session (including credentials), while Telnet transmits data, including usernames and passwords, in plaintext, making it vulnerable to eavesdropping
options.B: SSH cannot be used for CLI access, only for file transfer
options.C: They provide identical security, differing only in port number
options.D: Telnet encrypts sessions, and SSH does not

questions.explanation_es: SSH cifra toda la sesión, incluyendo las credenciales de acceso, mientras que Telnet transmite todo en texto plano (incluyendo usuario y contraseña), haciéndolo vulnerable a ser interceptado (eavesdropping) por cualquiera con acceso a la ruta de red. Por eso SSH es el estándar recomendado para gestión remota.

questions.name: AAA (TACACS+/RADIUS)
questions.question: Which transport protocol and port does TACACS+ use by default, as opposed to RADIUS?
