options.A: Both protocols use the exact same port and transport
options.B: TACACS+ uses HTTP as its transport
options.C: TACACS+ uses TCP port 49; RADIUS uses UDP ports 1812/1813 (authentication/accounting) — reflecting TACACS+'s reliance on TCP's connection-oriented delivery versus RADIUS's use of UDP
options.D: TACACS+ uses UDP port 49; RADIUS uses TCP ports 1812/1813

questions.explanation_es: TACACS+ utiliza TCP en el puerto 49, aprovechando la entrega orientada a conexión de TCP; RADIUS utiliza UDP, típicamente en los puertos 1812 (autenticación/autorización) y 1813 (accounting), reflejando un enfoque más liviano pero sin las garantías de entrega de TCP.

questions.name: ACLs
questions.question: What happens to a packet that does not match any explicit permit or deny statement in a Cisco ACL?

options.A: The packet causes the router to reboot
options.B: The ACL is automatically disabled
options.C: It is always permitted by default if no explicit match occurs
options.D: It is denied, due to the implicit 'deny any' at the end of every ACL, even though it is not visibly configured

questions.explanation_es: Toda ACL de Cisco tiene un 'deny any' implícito al final, aunque no aparezca explícitamente en la configuración; cualquier paquete que no coincida con ninguna sentencia permit/deny explícita configurada será denegado por este comportamiento implícito por defecto.

questions.name: ACLs
questions.question: What is a practical advantage of using named ACLs over numbered ACLs?

options.A: There is no functional difference between named and numbered ACLs
options.B: Named ACLs cannot be applied to any interface
options.C: Named ACLs allow individual entries to be added or removed (edited) more easily by line/sequence, and the name itself can be more descriptive of the ACL's purpose
options.D: Numbered ACLs support far more entries than named ACLs, which is their only advantage

questions.explanation_es: Las ACLs nombradas (named ACLs) permiten agregar o eliminar entradas individuales de forma más flexible (usando números de secuencia), sin tener que recrear toda la lista, además de que el nombre puede ser descriptivo del propósito de la ACL, facilitando su identificación y mantenimiento frente a una ACL puramente numerada.

questions.name: CoPP
questions.question: How does CoPP typically classify and treat different types of traffic destined to the control plane?

options.A: It applies a single identical policy to all traffic destined to the control plane, with no classification
options.B: It classifies traffic into different classes (e.g., critical/routing protocols, normal management traffic, undesirable/malicious traffic) and applies a different policy (permit, rate-limit, or drop) to each class
options.C: It only classifies traffic based on the physical interface, never by traffic type
options.D: CoPP cannot distinguish between different types of control-plane traffic

questions.explanation_es: CoPP típicamente clasifica el tráfico destinado al plano de control en distintas clases (por ejemplo, tráfico crítico como protocolos de enrutamiento, tráfico de gestión normal, y tráfico indeseable o potencialmente malicioso), aplicando una política diferenciada a cada clase (permitir, limitar la tasa, o descartar), en lugar de tratar todo el tráfico hacia la CPU de forma idéntica.

questions.name: Seguridad de REST API
questions.question: Why is using HTTPS (TLS) essential for securing REST API communications, such as those with Cisco Catalyst Center?

options.A: HTTPS eliminates the need for any authentication token
options.B: HTTPS is only relevant for browser-based access, not for API calls
options.C: HTTPS encrypts the data in transit between the client and the API server, protecting credentials, tokens, and payload data from being intercepted or tampered with over the network
options.D: HTTP and HTTPS provide identical security for API traffic

questions.explanation_es: HTTPS (HTTP sobre TLS) cifra los datos en tránsito entre el cliente y el servidor de la API, protegiendo credenciales, tokens de autenticación y datos del payload de ser interceptados o manipulados por un atacante en la red, algo que HTTP plano no ofrece.

questions.name: Seguridad de REST API
questions.question: What does the principle of 'least privilege' mean when applied to API access scopes/roles?

options.A: It means API calls should always be rate-limited to one request per minute
options.B: An API client or user should only be granted the minimum permissions/scopes necessary to perform its intended function, rather than broad or administrative access by default
options.C: Every API client should be granted full administrative access by default for convenience
options.D: Least privilege only applies to human users, never to API service accounts

questions.explanation_es: El principio de menor privilegio (least privilege) establece que a un cliente de API o usuario se le deben otorgar solo los permisos/scopes mínimos necesarios para cumplir su función prevista, en lugar de otorgar acceso amplio o administrativo por defecto, reduciendo el impacto potencial si esas credenciales son comprometidas.

questions.name: Threat defense
questions.question: What is the general purpose of a threat intelligence feed in a network security architecture?

options.A: It provides continuously updated information about known indicators of compromise (IoCs), malicious IPs/domains, and emerging threats, which security tools use to improve detection accuracy
options.B: It replaces the need for any firewall or IPS
options.C: It provides only historical data with no relevance to current threats
options.D: It is used exclusively for billing and licensing purposes

questions.explanation_es: Un feed de inteligencia de amenazas provee información continuamente actualizada sobre indicadores de compromiso conocidos (IoCs), direcciones IP/dominios maliciosos y amenazas emergentes, que las herramientas de seguridad (firewalls, IPS, etc.) utilizan para mejorar la precisión de la detección frente a amenazas actuales.

questions.name: Threat defense
questions.question: What is the core idea behind the 'zero trust' security model?

options.A: Once a device is inside the corporate network, it should be fully trusted with no further verification
options.B: No user, device, or system should be automatically trusted based solely on network location; every access request should be continuously verified regardless of whether it originates inside or outside the traditional network perimeter
options.C: Zero trust means disabling all authentication mechanisms
options.D: Zero trust only applies to external/internet-facing traffic, never internal traffic

questions.explanation_es: El modelo de zero trust (confianza cero) parte de la idea de que ningún usuario, dispositivo o sistema debe confiarse automáticamente solo por estar dentro del perímetro tradicional de la red; cada solicitud de acceso debe verificarse de forma continua, sin importar si el origen es interno o externo, reduciendo el riesgo de movimiento lateral tras una brecha.

questions.name: Seguridad de endpoint (NAC/ISE)
questions.question: In 802.1X port-based authentication, what are the three key roles involved?

options.A: Client, Server, and Firewall — with no other roles defined
options.B: Only two roles exist: Supplicant and Authenticator, with no separate Authentication Server
options.C: Router, Switch, and Access Point, with no client-side role
options.D: Supplicant (the client device requesting access), Authenticator (the switch/AP enforcing the port state), and Authentication Server (e.g., RADIUS server, which validates credentials)

questions.explanation_es: 802.1X define tres roles clave: el Supplicant (el dispositivo cliente que solicita acceso a la red), el Authenticator (típicamente el switch o access point, que controla el estado del puerto según el resultado de la autenticación), y el Authentication Server (por ejemplo, un servidor RADIUS/ISE, que valida las credenciales del supplicant).

questions.name: Seguridad de endpoint (NAC/ISE)
questions.question: What is the purpose of MAB (MAC Authentication Bypass) in a NAC deployment?

options.A: It is used only for wireless guest networks, never for wired ports
options.B: It completely replaces 802.1X for all devices, including those capable of doing 802.1X
options.C: It allows devices that cannot perform 802.1X authentication (such as printers or IoT devices) to be authenticated based on their MAC address instead, as a fallback mechanism
options.D: It disables all authentication for devices matching a MAC address whitelist without any verification

questions.explanation_es: MAB (MAC Authentication Bypass) permite que dispositivos incapaces de realizar autenticación 802.1X (como impresoras, cámaras IP, o ciertos dispositivos IoT) sean autenticados basándose en su dirección MAC como mecanismo alternativo (fallback), en lugar de quedar completamente sin acceso o requerir excepciones manuales complejas.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: What is the primary role of Cisco Firepower Management Center (FMC) in a Cisco NGFW deployment?

options.A: It provides centralized policy management, monitoring, and reporting for one or more Firepower Threat Defense (FTD) NGFW devices
options.B: It is used exclusively for wireless controller management
options.C: It is a hardware appliance that replaces the FTD firewall itself
options.D: It only manages licensing, with no policy or monitoring capability

questions.explanation_es: FMC (Firepower Management Center) provee gestión centralizada de políticas, monitoreo y reportes para uno o varios dispositivos NGFW Firepower Threat Defense (FTD), permitiendo administrar de forma consistente múltiples firewalls desde una única consola en lugar de configurarlos individualmente.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: What does Application Visibility and Control (AVC) provide within a Cisco NGFW or router?

options.A: Only the ability to see interface bandwidth utilization, with no application-level detail
options.B: AVC replaces the need for any firewall rules
options.C: AVC is used exclusively for physical cable diagnostics
options.D: The ability to identify specific applications generating traffic (beyond just port/protocol) and apply granular policy (allow, block, QoS treatment) based on that application identity

questions.explanation_es: AVC (Application Visibility and Control) permite identificar qué aplicación específica está generando cierto tráfico (más allá de simplemente el puerto/protocolo usado, ya que muchas apps modernas comparten puertos como 443), y aplicar políticas granulares (permitir, bloquear, dar cierto tratamiento de QoS) basadas en esa identidad de aplicación.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: In Python, what keyword is used to define a reusable function?

options.A: def
options.B: function
options.C: func
options.D: lambda is the only way to define any function

questions.explanation_es: En Python, una función se define usando la palabra clave 'def', seguida del nombre de la función y sus parámetros entre paréntesis, por ejemplo: 'def mi_funcion(parametro):'. 'lambda' se usa para funciones anónimas de una sola expresión, pero no es la forma estándar de definir una función reutilizable con nombre.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: Which of these data types is NOT natively supported directly by the JSON specification?

options.A: Comments (JSON has no native syntax for comments within the document)
options.B: Strings
options.C: Boolean values (true/false)
options.D: Numbers

questions.explanation_es: JSON no soporta comentarios de forma nativa dentro del documento; a diferencia de YAML u otros formatos, no existe una sintaxis estándar para agregar comentarios en un archivo JSON válido. Sí soporta strings, números, booleanos, null, objetos y arreglos.

questions.name: Códigos de respuesta REST API
questions.question: What is the key difference between an HTTP 401 Unauthorized and a 403 Forbidden response?

options.A: Both codes only apply to POST requests, never to GET requests
options.B: 401 indicates the request lacks valid authentication credentials (or they were rejected); 403 indicates the client is authenticated but does not have permission to access the requested resource
options.C: 403 means the credentials were invalid, and 401 means the user lacks permission despite being authenticated
options.D: 401 and 403 mean exactly the same thing and are used interchangeably

questions.explanation_es: 401 Unauthorized indica que la solicitud carece de credenciales de autenticación válidas (o fueron rechazadas) — el cliente no está autenticado correctamente. 403 Forbidden indica que el cliente SÍ está autenticado, pero no tiene permiso para acceder al recurso solicitado — es un problema de autorización, no de autenticación.

questions.name: Códigos de respuesta REST API
questions.question: When interpreting a paginated JSON response from an API (such as Catalyst Center's Intent APIs), what is a typical purpose of metadata fields often included in the response envelope?

options.A: To encrypt the response body
options.B: To store the API's licensing key
options.C: To indicate details such as whether more results exist beyond the current page, so the client knows whether to make additional requests to retrieve the full dataset
options.D: To specify which programming language the client must use

questions.explanation_es: En respuestas paginadas, los metadatos incluidos (por ejemplo, indicadores de si hay más resultados disponibles) le indican al cliente si debe realizar solicitudes adicionales para obtener el conjunto de datos completo, en lugar de asumir que la primera página contiene todos los resultados.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: What is a common 'action' type used within an EEM applet once a defined event triggers it?

options.A: EEM applets can only reboot the device as their sole possible action
options.B: Actions such as 'action X cli command' (to execute a CLI command) or 'action X syslog' (to generate a syslog message), used to automate a remediation or notification step
options.C: EEM applets cannot perform any actions, only detect events
options.D: Actions in EEM are limited to sending SNMP traps only

questions.explanation_es: Una vez que un evento definido dispara un applet EEM, se pueden configurar distintas acciones, como 'action X cli command' (para ejecutar un comando de CLI de forma automática) o 'action X syslog' (para generar un mensaje de syslog), permitiendo automatizar pasos de remediación, notificación, o recolección de datos de diagnóstico sin intervención manual.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: Why do agentless automation tools (like Ansible) tend to be particularly well-suited for managing network devices (routers, switches) compared to agent-based tools?

options.A: There is no practical difference between agent-based and agentless approaches for network devices
options.B: Agent-based tools are always faster and simpler to use on network devices than agentless tools
options.C: Most network devices do not support running third-party software agents, so agentless tools that connect via standard protocols (SSH, NETCONF, RESTCONF) fit naturally without requiring vendor support for an installed agent
options.D: Network devices always have full support for running any third-party agent software natively

questions.explanation_es: La mayoría de los dispositivos de red (routers, switches) no soportan la instalación de agentes de software de terceros como sí lo hacen los servidores; por eso las herramientas agentless (como Ansible), que se conectan usando protocolos estándar (SSH, NETCONF, RESTCONF) sin requerir un agente instalado, encajan naturalmente mejor para la automatización de infraestructura de red.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: What does it mean for the HTTP PUT method to be 'idempotent', and how does this compare to POST?

options.A: Both PUT and POST are always non-idempotent by definition
options.B: Idempotency has no defined meaning in the context of HTTP methods
options.C: PUT is never idempotent, while POST always is
options.D: Sending the same PUT request multiple times results in the same final state (the resource is simply replaced with the same content each time); POST is generally NOT idempotent, since repeating it may create multiple new resources

questions.explanation_es: Que PUT sea idempotente significa que enviar la misma solicitud PUT múltiples veces produce el mismo estado final (el recurso queda reemplazado con el mismo contenido cada vez, sin efectos adicionales acumulativos). POST generalmente NO es idempotente, ya que repetir la misma solicitud POST puede crear múltiples recursos nuevos (por ejemplo, múltiples entradas duplicadas) en lugar de producir el mismo resultado.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: Which statement best describes how Policy-Based Routing (PBR) makes forwarding decisions compared to standard destination-based routing?

options.A: PBR can forward packets based on criteria such as source address, packet size, or protocol, overriding the routing table before the normal lookup occurs
options.B: PBR requires BGP to be configured on the router
options.C: PBR only functions on Layer 2 switches
options.D: PBR only considers the destination IP address, exactly like the routing table

questions.explanation_es: PBR usa route-maps para clasificar el tráfico por múltiples criterios (IP origen, tamaño de paquete, protocolo, etc.) y aplicar un next-hop distinto al que indicaría la tabla de enrutamiento normal. Se evalúa antes de la búsqueda estándar en la RIB.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: In a PBR route-map, what is the difference between the 'set ip next-hop' and 'set ip default next-hop' commands?

options.A: 'set ip next-hop' only works with static routes
options.B: 'set ip default next-hop' overrides BGP routes only
options.C: They are functionally identical
options.D: 'set ip next-hop' forwards to the specified address unconditionally when the route-map matches, while 'set ip default next-hop' is used only as a fallback when the routing table has no explicit route for the destination

questions.explanation_es: 'set ip next-hop' fuerza el next-hop indicado sin importar la tabla de enrutamiento. 'set ip default next-hop' solo se usa como respaldo, cuando el router no tiene una ruta explícita hacia el destino más allá de la default.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: On which interface direction is Policy-Based Routing typically applied with the 'ip policy route-map' command?

options.A: Only on loopback interfaces
options.B: Inbound, before the normal routing table lookup is performed
options.C: Outbound, after the routing table lookup
options.D: It applies globally to the router regardless of interface

questions.explanation_es: PBR se aplica con 'ip policy route-map' en el sentido entrante de la interfaz; el router evalúa el route-map sobre el tráfico que ingresa, antes de hacer la búsqueda normal en la tabla de enrutamiento.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: A company wants traffic from the Finance subnet (10.10.10.0/24) to always exit via ISP-A, while all other traffic uses the normal default route via ISP-B, regardless of destination. Which technology best achieves this without changing destination-based routing for other traffic?

options.A: VRRP
options.B: A static default route
options.C: OSPF route redistribution
options.D: Policy-Based Routing matching source address 10.10.10.0/24

questions.explanation_es: PBR permite clasificar el tráfico según el origen (entre otros criterios) y forzar un next-hop distinto solo para ese tráfico, dejando el resto sujeto al enrutamiento normal — algo que una ruta estática o un protocolo de enrutamiento por destino no logran por sí solos.

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: What distinguishes PAT (Port Address Translation) from standard dynamic NAT?

options.A: PAT translates only the destination address, never the source
options.B: PAT requires a one-to-one mapping between inside and outside addresses
options.C: PAT allows multiple internal hosts to share a single public IP address by also translating the Layer 4 port number
options.D: PAT only works with UDP traffic

questions.explanation_es: PAT (NAT overload) traduce dirección IP y puerto, permitiendo que muchos hosts internos compartan una sola IP pública, distinguiéndose entre sí por el número de puerto de origen traducido.

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: In Cisco NAT terminology, what does the 'inside local' address represent?

options.A: The address of an outside host as seen from the inside network
options.B: The translated address of an outside host
options.C: The public IP address as seen from the outside network
options.D: The real, typically private IP address assigned to a host on the inside network before translation

questions.explanation_es: 'Inside local' es la dirección real (normalmente privada) del host interno, tal como aparece en la red interna antes de la traducción. 'Inside global' es esa misma dirección después de traducirse a una IP pública.

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: Which statement about static NAT is correct?

options.A: It cannot be used for servers that must be reachable from the internet
options.B: It creates a temporary one-to-one mapping only when traffic is initiated from the inside
options.C: It always requires PAT to function
options.D: It creates a permanent one-to-one mapping between an inside local and an inside global address, allowing outside hosts to initiate connections to the inside host

questions.explanation_es: El NAT estático crea un mapeo fijo 1:1 entre una IP interna y una IP pública, permitiendo que hosts externos inicien conexiones hacia el host interno (por ejemplo, un servidor web) — a diferencia del NAT dinámico o PAT, que dependen de que la conexión se inicie desde adentro.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: In HSRP, which router becomes the Active router by default?

options.A: Whichever router boots up last
options.B: The router with the lowest priority value
options.C: The router with the highest HSRP priority (default 100); if tied, the highest IP address on the HSRP interface breaks the tie
options.D: The router with the lowest IP address

questions.explanation_es: En HSRP, el router con mayor prioridad (por defecto 100) se convierte en el Active. Si hay empate en la prioridad, se decide por la IP más alta en la interfaz HSRP.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: Unlike HSRP, which is a Cisco proprietary protocol, VRRP has what key characteristic?

options.A: VRRP requires a dedicated virtual IP separate from all physical interfaces
options.B: VRRP is an IETF standard protocol and can use the real interface IP address of one of the group's routers as the virtual IP
options.C: VRRP only supports 2 routers per group
options.D: VRRP does not support preemption

questions.explanation_es: VRRP es un estándar IETF (RFC), y permite que uno de los routers del grupo use su propia IP física de interfaz como la IP virtual (ese router se vuelve el Master 'IP owner'), algo que HSRP no hace, ya que siempre usa una IP virtual separada.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What is the purpose of IGMP (Internet Group Management Protocol)?

options.A: To allow hosts on a local subnet to inform a directly connected router which multicast groups they wish to receive
options.B: To route multicast traffic between different subnets
options.C: To elect the Rendezvous Point in PIM sparse mode
options.D: To encrypt multicast traffic

questions.explanation_es: IGMP opera entre hosts y su router local (dentro de la misma subred) para que los hosts informen su interés en recibir tráfico de determinados grupos multicast. El enrutamiento multicast entre subredes lo hace PIM, no IGMP.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: In PIM Sparse Mode, what is the role of the Rendezvous Point (RP)?

options.A: It replaces the need for IGMP entirely
options.B: It is the only device allowed to send multicast traffic
options.C: It acts as a meeting point where multicast sources register and receivers initially join, before the network potentially shifts to a more optimal shortest-path tree
options.D: It is only used in PIM Dense Mode

questions.explanation_es: El RP en PIM-SM funciona como un punto de encuentro: las fuentes se registran ahí y los receptores se unen inicialmente al árbol compartido (RPT) a través del RP; luego el tráfico puede migrar al árbol de ruta más corta (SPT) hacia la fuente para mayor eficiencia.

questions.name: NTP/PTP
questions.question: What does the NTP stratum number indicate?

options.A: The number of hops a device is away from an authoritative time source (stratum 0), with lower stratum numbers indicating greater accuracy
options.B: The number of NTP servers configured
options.C: The encryption strength of the NTP session
options.D: The version of NTP being used

questions.explanation_es: El stratum indica cuántos saltos hay entre el dispositivo y una fuente de tiempo autoritativa (stratum 0, como un reloj atómico o GPS). Cuanto menor el número de stratum, más cercano (y en teoría más preciso) es el dispositivo respecto a la fuente original.

questions.name: NTP/PTP
questions.question: Compared to NTP, why is PTP (Precision Time Protocol, IEEE 1588) used in environments requiring extremely accurate time synchronization?

options.A: PTP only works over Layer 3 networks, while NTP is Layer 2 only
options.B: PTP does not require any master clock
options.C: PTP achieves sub-microsecond accuracy using hardware timestamping, while NTP typically only achieves millisecond-level accuracy
options.D: PTP is a Cisco-proprietary replacement for NTP

questions.explanation_es: PTP (IEEE 1588) usa timestamping por hardware en los dispositivos de red, logrando precisión de sub-microsegundos, mientras que NTP típicamente logra precisión del orden de milisegundos — por eso PTP se usa en entornos como telco o financiero que requieren sincronización extremadamente precisa.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Which statement about LACP (Link Aggregation Control Protocol) EtherChannel modes is correct?

options.A: A channel will form if at least one side is set to 'active' and the other side is set to 'active' or 'passive'; two 'passive' sides will never form a channel
options.B: Setting both ends to 'active' will not form a channel
options.C: LACP requires PAgP to be enabled first
options.D: 'passive' mode actively sends LACP packets to initiate negotiation

questions.explanation_es: LACP forma el canal si al menos un extremo está en modo 'active' (y el otro en 'active' o 'passive'). Si ambos extremos están en 'passive', ninguno inicia la negociación y el canal nunca se forma, porque 'passive' espera recibir paquetes LACP en lugar de enviarlos.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: Which Python data type is immutable and therefore commonly used as a dictionary key?

options.A: set
options.B: dict
options.C: tuple
options.D: list

questions.explanation_es: Las tuplas son inmutables, por lo que pueden usarse como claves de diccionario (los dicts requieren claves hashables). Las listas y los propios dicts son mutables y no son hashables, así que no pueden usarse como claves.

questions.name: Python básico

options.A: KeyError
options.B: unknown
options.C: status
options.D: None

questions.explanation_es: dict.get(key, default) retorna el valor default indicado si la clave no existe, en vez de lanzar KeyError como haría data["status"]. Como "status" no está en el dict, imprime "unknown".

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: In a Python script using the 'requests' library to call a REST API, which method sends an HTTP GET request?

options.A: requests.send()
options.B: requests.query()
options.C: requests.get()
options.D: requests.fetch()

questions.explanation_es: La librería requests usa requests.get(url) para solicitudes GET y requests.post() para POST. Las otras opciones no son métodos reales de la librería.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: Which of the following is valid JSON?

options.C: {name: "R1", vlan: 10}

questions.explanation_es: JSON exige comillas dobles para claves y strings; las comillas simples (B) y las claves sin comillas (A) no son válidas, y una coma final después del último elemento (D) tampoco lo es en JSON estricto.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: What Python type does the JSON value 'null' map to when parsed with json.loads()?

options.B: "" (empty string)
options.C: None
options.D: False

questions.explanation_es: Al parsear JSON en Python, el valor null se convierte en el objeto None, no en 0, cadena vacía ni False.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: Which JSON structure correctly represents an array of two interface objects?

options.A: {"interfaces": [{"name": "Gi0/1", "status": "up"}, {"name": "Gi0/2", "status": "down"}]}
options.B: {"interfaces": {"Gi0/1": "up", "Gi0/2": "down"}}
options.C: {"interfaces": ("Gi0/1": "up", "Gi0/2": "down")}
options.D: {"interfaces": ["Gi0/1", "up", "Gi0/2", "down"]}

questions.explanation_es: Un array JSON de objetos usa corchetes conteniendo objetos {} separados por comas. La opción A es un objeto (no array), la B mezcla claves y valores en una lista plana, y la D usa paréntesis, que no es sintaxis JSON válida.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: When integrating a traditional (non-fabric) campus network with an SD-Access fabric, which device role connects the two domains?

options.A: Fabric Edge Node
options.B: Control Plane Node
options.C: Fabric Border Node
options.D: Fabric WLC

questions.explanation_es: El Border Node es el punto de interoperabilidad entre la fabric SD-Access y las redes externas o tradicionales; traduce entre el encapsulado VXLAN/LISP de la fabric y el enrutamiento IP tradicional fuera de ella.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: A host in a traditional VLAN-based segment needs to reach a host inside an SD-Access fabric. Which statement is correct?

options.A: SD-Access cannot interoperate with traditional networks under any circumstances, requiring a full fabric-wide migration first
options.B: Traffic enters/exits the fabric through the Border Node, which translates between the fabric overlay and traditional routing/switching
options.C: The traditional host must also run LISP and register its own EID with the fabric's Map Server before any traffic can pass
options.D: The Control Plane Node performs all packet forwarding for external traffic, in addition to maintaining the host-tracking database

questions.explanation_es: El Border Node traduce el tráfico entre el overlay de la fabric (VXLAN con políticas basadas en SGT) y una red tradicional externa; el host tradicional no necesita ejecutar LISP ni ningún protocolo especial de la fabric.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: During a phased migration from a traditional 3-tier campus to SD-Access, which approach is commonly recommended?

options.A: Migrate site by site or IP pool by IP pool, using the Border Node to maintain connectivity between migrated and non-migrated segments
options.B: It is not possible to migrate incrementally; all switches must be replaced and reconfigured at the exact same time
options.C: Only wireless clients can be migrated to SD-Access; wired endpoints must remain on the traditional network permanently
options.D: Migrate the entire campus in a single maintenance window, converting every switch to fabric mode simultaneously

questions.explanation_es: Una migración típica hacia SD-Access se hace de forma incremental (por sitio, por IP pool o por switch), aprovechando el Border Node para mantener conectividad entre las partes ya migradas y las que siguen en la red tradicional, evitando un corte total.

questions.name: CoPP
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Control Plane Policing (CoPP)?

options.A: To load-balance traffic across multiple CPUs
options.B: To protect the router/switch CPU by rate-limiting or filtering traffic destined to the control plane
options.C: To perform NAT on control plane traffic
options.D: To encrypt traffic destined to the control plane

questions.explanation_es: CoPP protege el plano de control (la CPU del equipo) aplicando políticas de rate-limiting/filtrado sobre el tráfico dirigido a la propia CPU (SSH, routing protocols, SNMP, etc.), evitando que un exceso de tráfico o un ataque agote los recursos del procesador.

questions.name: CoPP
questions.question: In which direction does Control Plane Policing apply its policy?

options.A: To traffic between two VLANs on the same switch
options.B: Only to transit traffic passing through the device
options.C: Only to traffic sourced by the device toward external hosts
options.D: To traffic destined TO the device's control plane (the CPU itself)

questions.explanation_es: CoPP se aplica específicamente al tráfico destinado a la CPU del propio dispositivo (control plane), no al tráfico de tránsito que solo pasa por el plano de datos sin involucrar a la CPU.

questions.name: CoPP
questions.question: Which Cisco IOS mechanism is used to configure CoPP?

options.A: QoS marking with 'mls qos trust'
options.B: A service-policy applied under the 'control-plane' context, using class-maps and a policy-map
options.C: An access-list applied directly to a physical interface with 'ip access-group'
options.D: A VACL (VLAN ACL) configuration

questions.explanation_es: CoPP se configura definiendo class-maps para clasificar el tráfico, un policy-map con las acciones (police/drop), y aplicándolo con 'service-policy input <nombre>' bajo el contexto 'control-plane', que representa lógicamente a la CPU del dispositivo.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: Which of these automation tools is classified as agentless (no software needs to be installed on the managed device)?

options.A: Puppet
options.B: Chef
options.C: Ansible
options.D: SaltStack running in agent mode

questions.explanation_es: Ansible es agentless: se conecta a los dispositivos gestionados vía SSH o APIs sin instalar software permanente en ellos. Puppet y Chef típicamente requieren un agente instalado en el nodo gestionado.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: What is a key operational advantage of an agentless automation approach for network devices?

options.A: It guarantees real-time push notifications from every managed device
options.B: It eliminates the need for any credentials to connect to devices
options.C: It avoids installing, updating, and maintaining agent software on each device — useful since many network devices cannot run third-party agents
options.D: It always executes tasks faster than agent-based tools in every scenario

questions.explanation_es: Muchos dispositivos de red no pueden ejecutar software de terceros como un agente; el enfoque agentless evita esa necesidad, conectándose bajo demanda (SSH/API) sin instalar ni mantener nada persistente en el dispositivo.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: In an agent-based orchestration model (e.g., Puppet), what role does the agent play on the managed node?

options.A: It only serves as a passive log collector with no configuration capability
options.B: It only functions during initial provisioning and is then uninstalled
options.C: It runs persistently, periodically pulling configuration from a central server and applying it locally
options.D: It replaces the need for a central server entirely

questions.explanation_es: En un modelo basado en agentes, el agente se instala de forma persistente en el nodo gestionado y contacta periódicamente a un servidor central (master) para obtener y aplicar la configuración deseada.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Cisco Embedded Event Manager (EEM)?

options.A: To provide a GUI for network monitoring
options.B: To detect an event on a device (CLI command, syslog message, CPU threshold, etc.) and automatically trigger a defined action in response
options.C: To encrypt configuration files
options.D: To replace SNMP entirely

questions.explanation_es: EEM permite definir applets que combinan un evento disparador (event detector) con una acción automática a ejecutar en respuesta, como enviar un email, correr un comando o generar un log.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: Which EEM event detector triggers an applet when a specific CLI command is entered by a user?

options.A: event cli
options.B: event snmp
options.C: event timer
options.D: event syslog

questions.explanation_es: 'event cli' detecta cuando se ingresa un patrón de comando CLI específico (con 'match' sobre una expresión regular), disparando el applet antes o después de ejecutarse ese comando.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: An EEM applet is configured with 'event syslog pattern "%LINK-3-UPDOWN"' and an action to send an email. What triggers this applet?

options.A: A scheduled timer, regardless of any link event
options.B: The router generating a syslog message matching that pattern, such as an interface changing state
options.C: An SNMP trap received from another device
options.D: A manual CLI command entered by the administrator

questions.explanation_es: 'event syslog' dispara el applet cuando el dispositivo genera internamente un mensaje de syslog que coincide con el patrón indicado, en este caso un cambio de estado de una interfaz.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: In RESTful API design, which HTTP method is idempotent and used to completely replace an existing resource?

options.A: GET
options.B: PUT
options.C: POST
options.D: PATCH

questions.explanation_es: PUT reemplaza por completo el recurso indicado con el cuerpo enviado y es idempotente. POST no es idempotente (crea un nuevo recurso cada vez) y PATCH aplica una modificación parcial, no un reemplazo completo.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: Which HTTP method is typically used to apply a partial update to an existing resource, modifying only specific fields?

options.A: PATCH
options.B: DELETE
options.C: PUT
options.D: OPTIONS

questions.explanation_es: PATCH se usa para aplicar una modificación parcial a un recurso existente (cambiar solo algunos campos), a diferencia de PUT, que reemplaza el recurso completo.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: Which statement about the HTTP GET method is correct?

options.A: GET is the only method that can return a 201 Created status
options.B: GET requires a request body containing the resource data
options.C: GET is used to create new resources on the server
options.D: GET should be safe and idempotent, retrieving a representation of a resource without side effects on the server

questions.explanation_es: GET es un método seguro (no debería modificar el estado del servidor) e idempotente, usado para leer un recurso. Crear un recurso, que puede devolver 201 Created, es responsabilidad típica de POST.

questions.name: Seguridad de endpoint (NAC/ISE)
questions.question: In Cisco ISE, what is the primary function of a posture assessment?

options.A: To encrypt traffic between the endpoint and the switch
options.B: To check whether an endpoint complies with security policies (e.g., antivirus up to date, OS patches installed) before granting full network access
options.C: To determine the physical location of an endpoint
options.D: To assign a static IP address to the endpoint

questions.explanation_es: La evaluación de postura en ISE verifica que el endpoint cumpla los requisitos de seguridad definidos (antivirus, parches del SO, etc.) antes de otorgarle acceso completo; si no cumple, puede colocarse en una VLAN de cuarentena o remediación.

questions.name: Seguridad de endpoint (NAC/ISE)
questions.question: Before 802.1X authentication completes, what kind of access does a switch port typically allow the connecting endpoint?

options.A: Trunk-level access to all VLANs
options.B: No traffic of any kind, including DHCP
options.C: Full, unrestricted access to the network
options.D: Restricted access via a pre-authentication ACL, allowing only what's needed for the authentication process itself (e.g., DHCP, ISE communication)

questions.explanation_es: Antes de completarse la autenticación 802.1X, el puerto suele permitir un acceso restringido mediante una ACL de pre-autenticación, habilitando solo el tráfico necesario para el propio proceso (DHCP, DNS, comunicación con ISE), no acceso completo.

questions.name: AAA (TACACS+/RADIUS)
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes TACACS+ from RADIUS?

options.A: TACACS+ encrypts the entire packet body, while RADIUS encrypts only the password field
options.B: Both encrypt the entire packet identically
options.C: TACACS+ encrypts only the password in the packet, while RADIUS encrypts the entire packet body
options.D: Neither protocol encrypts any part of the packet

questions.explanation_es: TACACS+ cifra todo el cuerpo del paquete, mientras que RADIUS solo cifra el campo de contraseña, dejando el resto del paquete (como el username) sin cifrar.

questions.name: AAA (TACACS+/RADIUS)
questions.question: Which AAA protocol separates authentication and authorization into distinct processes, making it well suited for granular per-command authorization on network devices?

options.A: LDAP
options.B: TACACS+
options.C: Kerberos
options.D: RADIUS

questions.explanation_es: TACACS+ separa claramente autenticación, autorización y accounting en procesos independientes, permitiendo un control granular como autorizar comandos individuales en el CLI — algo que RADIUS, al combinar autenticación y autorización, no maneja tan bien.

questions.name: ACLs
questions.question: In a standard IPv4 ACL, which criterion can be used to match traffic?

options.A: Source IP address only
options.B: Source and destination IP address plus Layer 4 port
options.C: VLAN tag
options.D: Destination MAC address

questions.explanation_es: Las ACL estándar de IPv4 solo pueden filtrar según la dirección IP de origen. Para filtrar por IP destino, protocolo o puertos de Capa 4 se necesita una ACL extendida.

questions.name: ACLs
questions.question: By default, what happens to a packet that matches no explicit statement in an ACL applied to an interface?

options.A: It is denied, due to an implicit 'deny all' at the end of every ACL
options.B: It is queued until an administrator manually decides
options.C: It is permitted, since ACLs default to permit
options.D: It is forwarded using the next ACL in sequence

questions.explanation_es: Toda ACL de Cisco tiene una sentencia implícita de 'deny all' al final (aunque no se muestre en la configuración), por lo que el tráfico que no coincide explícitamente con un 'permit' se descarta.

questions.name: Threat defense
questions.question: What is the primary advantage of a Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW) compared to a traditional stateful firewall?

options.A: NGFW cannot perform stateful inspection
options.B: NGFW is only used for wireless networks
options.C: NGFW adds capabilities like application awareness and integrated intrusion prevention on top of traditional stateful filtering
options.D: NGFW only filters based on source/destination IP and port, exactly like a traditional firewall

questions.explanation_es: Un NGFW mantiene la inspección con estado tradicional pero suma capacidades como reconocimiento de aplicaciones (más allá del puerto) y prevención de intrusiones (IPS) integrada, no solo filtrado por IP/puerto.

questions.name: Threat defense
questions.question: In the context of threat defense, what does 'defense in depth' refer to?

options.A: Relying exclusively on user training to prevent attacks
options.B: Using a single, very powerful firewall as the sole security control
options.C: Applying multiple, layered security controls so that if one layer fails, others still provide protection
options.D: Encrypting data at rest only

questions.explanation_es: 'Defense in depth' es la estrategia de aplicar múltiples capas de seguridad complementarias (perimetral, segmentación interna, endpoint, monitoreo), de forma que ningún punto único de falla comprometa toda la red.

questions.name: Seguridad de REST API
questions.question: Which authentication mechanism involves the client sending a token in the 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' HTTP header on each API request?

options.A: Basic authentication with username/password on every request
options.C: IPsec
options.D: OAuth 2.0 token-based authentication

questions.explanation_es: En OAuth 2.0, tras autenticarse el cliente recibe un token de acceso que envía en el header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' en cada solicitud posterior, sin reenviar usuario/contraseña cada vez.

questions.name: Seguridad de REST API
questions.question: Why is HTTPS (TLS) considered essential for securing REST API calls that carry authentication credentials or tokens?

options.A: HTTPS encrypts the data in transit, preventing credentials/tokens from being intercepted in cleartext
options.B: HTTPS replaces the need for any authentication mechanism
options.C: HTTPS makes the API respond faster
options.D: HTTPS is only needed for GET requests

questions.explanation_es: HTTPS cifra el tráfico entre cliente y servidor, protegiendo credenciales y tokens de ser interceptados en texto plano (por ejemplo en un ataque man-in-the-middle); no reemplaza la autenticación, la complementa.

questions.name: IP SLA
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Cisco IP SLA?

options.A: To actively generate synthetic traffic and measure network performance metrics such as latency, jitter, and packet loss
options.B: To assign IP addresses dynamically to hosts
options.C: To encrypt traffic between two IP SLA-enabled routers
options.D: To perform routing between VLANs

questions.explanation_es: IP SLA genera tráfico sintético (probes) entre dispositivos para medir activamente métricas de rendimiento como latencia, jitter, pérdida de paquetes y disponibilidad, útil para monitoreo proactivo.

questions.name: IP SLA
questions.question: How can IP SLA be combined with object tracking to improve network resiliency?

options.A: IP SLA automatically reconfigures BGP neighbor relationships
options.B: IP SLA replaces the need for a routing protocol entirely
options.C: IP SLA cannot be combined with any other feature
options.D: A 'track' object can monitor an IP SLA operation and trigger actions like removing a static route from the routing table if the tracked path fails

questions.explanation_es: Un objeto 'track' puede monitorear el estado de una operación de IP SLA (por ejemplo, alcanzabilidad de un gateway) y, si falla, disparar acciones automáticas como retirar una ruta estática, logrando una conmutación por falla más rápida.

questions.name: Flexible NetFlow
questions.question: In Flexible NetFlow, what is the role of a flow exporter?

options.A: It stores historical flow records permanently on the router
options.B: It defines the destination (IP address and port) and transport used to send exported flow data to a collector
options.C: It applies the flow monitor to an interface
options.D: It defines which fields are used as match/key fields for identifying a flow

questions.explanation_es: El flow exporter configura hacia dónde (IP/puerto del collector) y cómo (por ejemplo, NetFlow v9 o IPFIX) se envían los registros de flujo, separado de qué campos componen cada flujo, que define el flow record.

questions.name: Flexible NetFlow
questions.question: Which components must be configured and associated to enable Flexible NetFlow on an interface?

options.A: Only an access-list applied to the interface
options.B: A route-map and a class-map
options.C: A flow record and a flow monitor (with an optional flow exporter), with the flow monitor applied to the interface
options.D: A SPAN session and a VLAN ACL

questions.explanation_es: Flexible NetFlow se arma con un flow record (define qué campos se recolectan) y un flow monitor (asocia el record con una caché, opcionalmente con un exporter) que se aplica a la interfaz; el exporter es opcional para enviar los datos a un collector externo.

questions.name: SPAN/RSPAN/ERSPAN
questions.question: What is the key difference between SPAN and RSPAN?

options.A: There is no functional difference; RSPAN is just a newer name for SPAN
options.B: SPAN can span traffic across multiple switches using a dedicated VLAN, while RSPAN cannot
options.C: RSPAN can mirror traffic across multiple switches over a dedicated RSPAN VLAN, while SPAN is limited to a single switch
options.D: SPAN encrypts mirrored traffic; RSPAN does not

questions.explanation_es: SPAN copia tráfico de un puerto/VLAN origen a un puerto destino dentro del mismo switch. RSPAN extiende esa capacidad usando una VLAN dedicada para transportar el tráfico espejado a través de múltiples switches.

questions.name: SPAN/RSPAN/ERSPAN
questions.question: Why would an administrator choose ERSPAN over SPAN or RSPAN?

options.A: ERSPAN cannot be used with Cisco Catalyst switches
options.B: ERSPAN is required whenever mirroring traffic within the same switch
options.C: ERSPAN only works on a single VLAN within one switch
options.D: ERSPAN encapsulates the mirrored traffic in GRE, allowing it to be transported over a routed Layer 3 network to a remote destination

questions.explanation_es: ERSPAN encapsula el tráfico espejado en GRE, permitiendo enviarlo a través de una red enrutada de Capa 3 hacia un destino remoto (por ejemplo, una herramienta de monitoreo en otro sitio), algo que SPAN y RSPAN no pueden hacer al estar limitados a Capa 2.

questions.name: Líneas y autenticación local
questions.question: Which command creates a local username/password database entry for authentication on a Cisco device?

options.A: username admin password Cisco123
options.B: enable secret Cisco123
options.C: line vty 0 4
options.D: aaa new-model

questions.explanation_es: El comando 'username <nombre> password <clave>' crea una entrada en la base de datos local de usuarios del dispositivo, usada para autenticación local en líneas configuradas con 'login local'.

questions.name: Líneas y autenticación local
questions.question: What is the effect of the 'login local' command applied under 'line vty 0 4'?

options.A: It requires users connecting via those VTY lines to authenticate using the local username database configured on the device
options.B: It forces authentication exclusively through a RADIUS server
options.C: It disables authentication entirely for VTY lines
options.D: It applies only to console line access, not VTY

questions.explanation_es: 'login local' bajo las líneas VTY indica que la autenticación debe validarse contra la base de datos local de usuarios (creada con 'username'), en lugar de usar solo una contraseña de línea genérica o un servidor AAA externo.

questions.name: NETCONF/RESTCONF
questions.question: Which transport protocol does NETCONF use by default?

options.A: Telnet
options.B: HTTP
options.C: HTTPS
options.D: SSH

questions.explanation_es: NETCONF (RFC 6241) se transporta típicamente sobre SSH (puerto 830 por defecto), a diferencia de RESTCONF, que usa HTTP/HTTPS.

questions.name: NETCONF/RESTCONF
questions.question: Which encoding format does NETCONF use to structure its messages, such as <get-config> and <edit-config> operations?

options.A: Only plain text
options.B: CSV
options.C: XML
options.D: Only JSON

questions.explanation_es: NETCONF utiliza XML para codificar sus mensajes y operaciones, a diferencia de RESTCONF, que soporta tanto XML como JSON.

questions.name: Catalyst Center
questions.question: Which Cisco Catalyst Center (formerly DNA Center) feature provides end-to-end visibility into network health and can proactively identify issues affecting client connectivity?

options.A: Assurance
options.B: Path Trace
options.C: Template Editor
options.D: Plug and Play

questions.explanation_es: Assurance en Catalyst Center recopila telemetría de la red y los clientes para dar visibilidad de salud end-to-end, detectando proactivamente problemas y sugiriendo posibles causas raíz.

questions.name: Catalyst Center
questions.question: What does the Catalyst Center 'Path Trace' tool do?

options.A: It simulates and traces the actual path a packet would take between two endpoints, showing each hop and potential issues along the way
options.B: It automatically remediates any configuration errors found
options.C: It only shows historical CPU utilization graphs
options.D: It is used exclusively for wireless site surveys

questions.explanation_es: Path Trace traza la ruta real (hop por hop) que seguiría o está siguiendo el tráfico entre un origen y un destino, mostrando el estado de cada salto y ayudando a identificar dónde ocurre un problema.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: What is the role of Cisco Firepower Management Center (FMC) in relation to NGFW/FTD devices?

options.A: FMC replaces the need for any firewall policy configuration
options.B: FMC is a centralized management platform used to configure policies, monitor events, and manage multiple NGFW/FTD devices from one place
options.C: FMC only performs DNS resolution for the NGFW
options.D: FMC is installed directly on each NGFW device with no separate management platform

questions.explanation_es: FMC es la plataforma de gestión centralizada desde la cual se configuran políticas, se monitorean eventos y se administran múltiples dispositivos NGFW/FTD, en lugar de configurar cada uno individualmente.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: What does Application Visibility and Control (AVC) primarily provide on a Cisco network device?

options.A: Encryption of all application traffic
options.B: DNS-based load balancing between applications
options.C: Automatic patching of vulnerable applications
options.D: The ability to identify applications traversing the network (via NBAR2) and apply policies such as QoS marking or blocking based on that application

questions.explanation_es: AVC combina NBAR2 para identificar aplicaciones específicas en el tráfico (más allá del puerto) con la capacidad de aplicar políticas —como QoS o bloqueo— basadas en esa aplicación identificada.

questions.name: VMs / FT / DRS
questions.question: In a virtualized environment (e.g., VMware vSphere), what does Fault Tolerance (FT) provide?

options.A: Automatic load balancing of VMs across hosts based on resource usage
options.B: A live, continuously synchronized secondary copy of a VM on a different host, which takes over instantly with zero downtime if the primary host fails
options.C: Scheduled nightly backups of VM disk images
options.D: Encryption of VM network traffic

questions.explanation_es: Fault Tolerance mantiene una VM secundaria sincronizada en tiempo real en otro host; si el host primario falla, la secundaria toma el control de inmediato sin pérdida de estado — a diferencia de HA, que reinicia la VM tras la falla.

questions.name: VMs / FT / DRS
questions.question: What is the purpose of Distributed Resource Scheduler (DRS) in a virtualization cluster?

options.A: It performs VM backups automatically
options.B: It automatically balances VM workloads across hosts in a cluster by migrating VMs to optimize resource utilization
options.C: It manages physical firewall rules
options.D: It provides zero-downtime failover identical to Fault Tolerance

questions.explanation_es: DRS monitorea el uso de recursos de los hosts en un clúster y migra VMs automáticamente (vía migración en vivo) entre hosts para balancear la carga, sin proveer la tolerancia a fallas instantánea que sí ofrece FT.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: What distinguishes a Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisor from a Type 2 (hosted) hypervisor?

options.A: Type 1 requires a host OS to function; Type 2 does not
options.B: There is no meaningful architectural difference between them
options.C: Type 2 hypervisors always provide better performance than Type 1
options.D: Type 1 runs directly on the physical hardware; Type 2 runs as an application on top of a host operating system

questions.explanation_es: Un hypervisor tipo 1 (bare-metal, como VMware ESXi) se ejecuta directamente sobre el hardware físico sin un sistema operativo host intermedio. Un tipo 2 se ejecuta como aplicación dentro de un SO host ya existente, agregando overhead.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: Why are Type 1 hypervisors generally preferred in enterprise data center environments over Type 2 hypervisors?

options.A: Type 1 hypervisors offer better performance and lower overhead since they interact directly with hardware, without an extra host OS layer
options.B: Type 2 hypervisors cannot run more than one VM at a time
options.C: Type 1 hypervisors are always free of charge
options.D: Type 1 hypervisors do not support live migration

questions.explanation_es: Al ejecutarse directamente sobre el hardware sin un sistema operativo host de por medio, los hypervisors tipo 1 tienen menor overhead y mejor rendimiento, por lo que son preferidos en centros de datos que ejecutan múltiples VMs de producción.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of VRF (Virtual Routing and Forwarding)?

options.A: To encrypt traffic between two routers
options.B: To maintain multiple independent routing tables on a single router, allowing overlapping IP address spaces and traffic isolation between virtual networks
options.C: To load-balance traffic across multiple physical interfaces
options.D: To compress routing table entries to save memory

questions.explanation_es: VRF permite que un mismo router mantenga múltiples tablas de enrutamiento independientes, aislando el tráfico entre distintos clientes o departamentos y permitiendo reutilizar los mismos rangos de IP sin conflicto.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: For two devices in different VRFs on the same router to communicate with each other, what is typically required?

options.A: Both devices must be in the same VLAN
options.B: VRF automatically bridges all instances at Layer 2
options.C: Route leaking (importing/exporting routes between VRFs) or an intermediate device connecting them, since VRFs are isolated by design
options.D: Nothing extra; VRFs communicate with each other by default

questions.explanation_es: Las VRFs están aisladas entre sí por diseño; para que se comuniquen se necesita una técnica explícita como route leaking (por ejemplo vía route-targets con MP-BGP) o un dispositivo intermedio como un firewall.

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: In LISP (Locator/ID Separation Protocol), what do the EID and RLOC represent?

options.A: EID is used only for IPv6 and RLOC only for IPv4
options.B: RLOC identifies the device's identity, while EID identifies its location
options.C: EID and RLOC are two names for the same address
options.D: EID identifies the device's identity, while RLOC identifies where that device is topologically reachable

questions.explanation_es: LISP separa identidad y ubicación: el EID identifica quién es el dispositivo (no cambia aunque se mueva), mientras que el RLOC identifica dónde está topológicamente alcanzable (el router de borde que lo conecta a la red de tránsito).

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: What is the role of the LISP Map Server/Map Resolver system?

options.A: It replaces the need for BGP in the underlay entirely
options.B: It performs NAT translation for LISP traffic
options.C: It encrypts LISP-encapsulated packets
options.D: It maintains and answers mapping queries between EIDs and their current RLOCs, similar in concept to how DNS maps names to IP addresses

questions.explanation_es: El sistema Map Server/Map Resolver mantiene la base de datos de mapeos EID-a-RLOC y resuelve consultas sobre dónde está alcanzable un EID, de forma conceptualmente similar a cómo DNS resuelve nombres a direcciones IP.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Which statement about GRE (Generic Routing Encapsulation) tunnels is correct?

options.A: GRE provides encryption of the encapsulated payload by default
options.B: GRE encapsulates a wide variety of protocols (including multicast and non-IP protocols) inside an IP packet, but provides no encryption on its own
options.C: GRE requires IPsec to function at all
options.D: GRE can only encapsulate TCP traffic

questions.explanation_es: GRE encapsula una amplia variedad de protocolos (incluido tráfico multicast) dentro de paquetes IP, creando un túnel; pero por sí solo no cifra ni autentica el tráfico, por eso suele combinarse con IPsec.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Why is GRE often combined with IPsec (GRE over IPsec) instead of using IPsec alone for certain deployments?

options.A: Because GRE is required for IPsec to establish a Security Association
options.B: Because IPsec alone cannot transport multicast or dynamic routing protocol traffic well, while GRE can encapsulate that traffic before IPsec encrypts it
options.C: Because IPsec cannot encrypt any IP traffic without GRE
options.D: Because GRE improves the encryption strength of IPsec

questions.explanation_es: IPsec en modo túnel puro no soporta bien tráfico multicast ni protocolos de enrutamiento dinámico que dependen de multicast (como OSPF). GRE puede encapsular ese tráfico dentro de un túnel IP unicast que luego IPsec cifra, combinando la flexibilidad de GRE con la seguridad de IPsec.

questions.name: Diagnóstico (debug/traceroute/ping/SNMP/syslog)
questions.question: Which statement about the 'debug' command on a Cisco IOS device is correct?

options.A: 'debug' commands permanently alter the device's running configuration
options.B: 'debug' output is only visible via SNMP
options.C: 'debug' commands can consume significant CPU resources and should be used cautiously in production, narrowed and disabled promptly after troubleshooting
options.D: 'debug' commands have no impact on device CPU and can always be left running safely

questions.explanation_es: Los comandos 'debug' generan y procesan mucha información en tiempo real, lo que puede consumir CPU significativa; se recomienda acotarlos (por ejemplo con listas de acceso) y desactivarlos ('undebug all') apenas se termina el troubleshooting.

questions.name: Códigos de respuesta REST API
questions.question: What does an HTTP 204 No Content response typically indicate?

options.A: The requested resource was permanently moved
options.B: The request failed due to a client error
options.C: The server is temporarily unavailable
options.D: The request succeeded, but there is no content to return in the response body (common after a successful DELETE)

questions.explanation_es: HTTP 204 No Content indica que la solicitud se procesó exitosamente pero no hay contenido para devolver — es común, por ejemplo, como respuesta a un DELETE exitoso donde no hace falta retornar datos.
